The four assembled works constitute an exceptionally productive nineteenth-century archive of mathematical astronomy, celestial photometry, dynamical systems, ancient cosmological interpretation, optical engineering, and natural philosophy. Their intellectual significance arises especially from the manner in which Proctor studies phenomena separated by immense differences in scale: an almost imperceptible displacement of a spectral line; the minute gravitational disturbance of a satellite; the apparent extinction of a star behind a Saturnian ring; the emergence of an ancient astronomical symbol on an Assyrian cylinder; the motion of sunlight across a lunar hemisphere; and the transmission of energetic disturbances from the solar photosphere into terrestrial magnetism.

Each phenomenon supplies an avenue into an invisible order of relations whose operations may be recovered through geometry, periodicity, instrumental mediation, or the comparison of apparently remote effects.

The investigation becomes especially remarkable when the four books are read together. In The Expanse of Heaven, Proctor develops an expansive cosmography in which stellar plurality, coloured suns, optical limitation, celestial distances, and the possibility of forms of perception exceeding human sight appear beside explicit theological reflections upon the Creator and His angelic ministers. In Saturn and Its System, astronomical calculation becomes a study of collective orbital behaviour, travelling waves within particulate rings, recurrent eclipse geometry, Chaldean astronomical periods, Assyrian representations, and ancient religious accounts of celestial power. In The Sun, spectroscopic engineering discloses metallic vapours in a remote luminous body, while solar outbursts and electrical disturbances on Earth establish the necessity of examining physical processes across planetary distances. In The Moon, lunar motion, illumination, relief, visibility, and the construction of an extraterrestrial observer's heavens permit the terrestrial world itself to become an astronomical object seen from beyond its ordinary human horizon.

The resulting Pro-metary establishes several interconnected research territories. Theo-teleology concerns the interpretation of ordered celestial phenomena in relation to divine purpose. Ontic-atavistic astronomy investigates the survival of ancient observations, technical ideas, and symbolic structures within subsequent cosmological traditions. Supernatural aetiology supplies the theological and historical examination of divine and angelic agency described in sacred texts. Metaphysical ontology asks how the existence of an object differs from its availability to a particular observer. Proto-astrophysical instrumentation reconstructs the means by which invisible physical properties become knowable through their observable consequences.

A particularly striking passage occurs in The Expanse of Heaven, original page 204, PDF page 271. Proctor considers possible sensory capacities far exceeding human sight and remarks that wonders inaccessible to us may nevertheless be apparent to the angels and ministers of the Creator. This passage merits sustained analysis alongside Colossians 1:16, which speaks of visible and invisible created orders, and the heavenly assemblies described in Job 38 and Revelation 4–5.

The strongest methodological opportunity lies in studying the limits of observation, the actuality of the unseen, and the authority of divine knowledge as three distinguishable but corresponding fields.

Proctor supplies the astronomical argument. Scripture supplies the metaphysical and theological testimony. Their comparison offers the foundation for an original investigation into the plurality of created orders without making their modes of existence identical.

🔑📜 Original scholarly contributions arising from the combined corpus

Contribution I. Biblical metallurgy as an astronomical indexing structure. Proctor's footnote on Numbers 31:22 provides a rare opportunity to construct a three-part concordance among Hebrew metal names, traditional planetary associations, and nineteenth-century astronomical interpretation. The initial research contribution is a comparative source apparatus, not an assertion that the biblical author intended an astronomical table.

Contribution II. The collective mechanics of the Saturnian ring system. Proctor's distinction between the motion of individual ring constituents and the propagation of larger-scale disturbances furnishes material for an unusually precise history of particulate celestial dynamics. 

This deserves comparison with mathematical theories of density waves, angular-momentum redistribution, and gravitationally disturbed discs.

Contribution III. A Chaldean astronomical technology dossier. The Nimrud lens, cuneiform records, cylinder impressions, eclipse periods, and Assyrian astronomical symbols should be assembled into one technical dossier, with their individual archaeological provenances and interpretations identified. 

Proctor's hypotheses can then be compared with those of Austen Henry Layard, Sir David Brewster, and subsequent Assyriologists.

Contribution IV. A mathematical history of eclipse recurrence. Proctor's account of the Saros permits comparison between ancient periodic calculation, lunar orbital geometry, and the precision of modern eclipse prediction. The distinction among synodic, nodical or draconic, anomalistic, and sidereal periods will be central to the mathematical apparatus.

Contribution V. The solar-electrical continuum. The nineteenth-century observations of solar eruptions, auroras, magnetic disturbances, and failures in telegraph equipment offer a well-documented physical chain linking celestial activity and terrestrial technology. This provides a substantial historical foundation for studying the measurement and consequences of space-weather phenomena.

Contribution VI. Spectroscopy as remote chemical investigation. Proctor's descriptions of prism batteries, dark spectral lines, vapour absorption, and the chemical constitution of the Sun connect instrumental engineering directly with the investigation of matter beyond Earth. A specialized study could reconstruct his observational methods and compare their principles with modern spectral analysis.

Contribution VII. Extraterrestrial observational geometry. Proctor's descriptions of the heavens as seen from the Moon and Saturn permit the construction of a historical comparative cosmography in which horizon, latitude, axial orientation, illumination, and apparent celestial motion are recalculated for different observers. This is especially valuable for the antipodes and sacred-geography research.

Contribution VIII. Ancient planetary worship and prophetic confrontation. Proctor's treatment of Assyrian and Chaldean celestial religion can be brought into close comparison with the Hebrew prophetic judgments upon foreign gods. The study will preserve distinct textual categories for named deities, sculptured representations, heavenly beings, and angelic interventions. The result should be a much more precise theological and historical apparatus than a generalized comparison of mythology and astronomy.

Contribution IX. A historical atlas of celestial misidentification. The four works contain material on apparent changes caused by optical contrast, instrumental limitation, photographic development, and celestial positioning. These cases can be gathered into an original historical atlas showing how observational techniques influence the interpretation of extraordinary physical phenomena.

Contribution X. The history of the mathematical material removed from The Moon. In the preface to the second edition, Proctor explains that he removed portions of the more demanding lunar theory and intended to republish them separately. 

This provides an important bibliographical warning: the 1878 volume is not identical in mathematical content to its predecessor. A future edition comparison could recover the omitted material and reconstruct the fuller mathematical apparatus.

Published: 10 October 1996
Russian documents Set out 'tectonic weapon' research
Carl Levitin

Moscow. The first official details have emerged in Moscow of ambitious research into 'tectonic warfare' carried out by the former Soviet Union and subsequently by the government of Russia, and involving atte mpts to stimulate 'artificial' earthquakes as weapons of destruction. According to documents obtained by the newspaper Moscow News, two research programmes, the first known as ' Mercury ' and the second as ' Volcano', were aimed at creating new earthquake epicentres by using underground nuclear explosions . Geophysicists are aware that impending earthquakes may be triggered by underground nuclear explosions . But Western geophysicists remain sceptical about tectonic warfare and have all but abandoned research after two unsuccessful phases of activity in the 1960s and 1980s, says Roger Clark, a lecturer in geophysics at the University of Leeds. Clark is not at all surprised that th e Russians tried to create earthquakes and control their location electromagnetically, however. "This sort of science is very much part of their heritage. We don't think it is impossible, or wrong , but past experience suggests it is very, very unlikely. "

The programme , which was secretly launched by the Communist rulers of the former Soviet Union in 1987, and has been unofficially known to Western geophysicists for several years, is now believed to have been abandoned. Russian documents Set out 'tectonic weapon' research
Carl Levitin

Moscow. The first official details have emerged in Moscow of ambitious research into 'tectonic warfare' carried out by the former Soviet Union and subsequently by the government of Russia, and involving atte mpts to stimulate 'artificial' earthquakes as weapons of destruction. According to documents obtained by the newspaper Moscow News, two research programmes, the first known as ' Mercury ' and the second as ' Volcano', were aimed at creating new earthquake epicentres by using underground nuclear explosions . Geophysicists are aware that impending earthquakes may be triggered by underground nuclear explosions . But Western geophysicists remain sceptical about tectonic warfare and have all but abandoned research after two unsuccessful phases of activity in the 1960s and 1980s, says Roger Clark, a lecturer in geophysics at the University of Leeds. Clark is not at all surprised that th e Russians tried to create earthquakes and control their location electromagnetically, however. "This sort of science is very much part of their heritage. We don't think it is impossible, or wrong , but past experience suggests it is very, very unlikely. "

The programme , which was secretly launched by the Communist rulers of the former Soviet Union in 1987, and has been unofficially known to Western geophysicists for several years, is now believed to have been abandoned. It would certainly contravene the terms of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, which Russia signed at the United Nations in Geneva last month . The Mercury project was launched in the former Soviet republic of Azerbaijan, but came to a halt when the republic became independent. It was superseded by the Volcano project. Three underground nuclear tests are believed to have taken place at sites in Kyrgyzstan.

According to the documents, the Mercury project was launched by a secret decree of the Central Committee of the Communist Party and the Council of Ministers of the Soviet Union. The objective was to "develop a methodology for remote operation on an earthquake epicentre by using weak seismic fields and research possibilities of transferring the seismic energy of an explosion ".

The documents say that the Mercury project involved 22 scientific and industrial organizations, including the Geological Institute of the Azerbaijan Academy of Sciences in Baku. The remit extended to developing the electronic equipment to be installed aboard space satellites that would control the tectonic weapon. The scientists were given three years to complete research, with testing planned for 1990.

During the research phase, Azerbaijani scientists grew increasingly confident and, according to the documents, were sure that " after [a] nuclear explosion, subterranean energy may accumulate at huge distances from the epicentre and reach massive capacity, after which the next directed explosion can release it all ".

Underground testing began at the town of Batken in Kyrgyzstan, and was directed by lkram Ke rimov , of the Azerbaijan Academy of Sciences. The documents say that scientists detonated an underground nuclear charge and tried to control the direction of seismic energy release d using British-built equipment known as 'system 9690 ' .

A report prepared by the Mozhaisky Military Engineering Institute concluded that the test had been a success. But progress slowed considerably following Azerbaijan's independence from the Soviet Union. At about this time , Russia embarked on a more comprehensive tectonic warfare programme known as the Volcano project. The Earth Physics Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences (RAS) became the project headquarters .

Research was scheduled to be completed in 1992, with underground testing beginning the following year. The final test was carried out at a place code-named S36NZ-0Kh; Moscow News believes the letters 'NZ' refer to Novaya Zemlya, where Soviet nuclear testing began in the 1950s."

Defense Primer: Directed-Energy Weapons
Both the 2022 National Defense Strategy and the House Armed Services Committee’s bipartisan Future of Defense Task Force Report have identified directed energy as a technology that could have a significant impact on U.S. national security in the years to come. As the Department of Defense (DOD) continues to invest in directed-energy (DE) weapons, Congress may consider implications for defense authorizations, appropriations, and oversight. Overview DOD defines DE weapons as those using concentrated electromagnetic energy, rather than kinetic energy, to “incapacitate, damage, disable, or destroy enemy equipment, facilities, and/or personnel.” DE weapons include high-energy lasers (HEL) and high-powered microwave (HPM) weapons; other DE weapons, such as particle beam weapons, are outside the scope of this In Focus. HELs might be used by ground forces in short-range air defense (SHORAD), counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS), or counter-rocket, artillery, and mortar (C-RAM) missions. The weapons might be used to “dazzle” (i.e., temporarily disable) or damage satellites and sensors. This could in turn interfere with intelligence-gathering operations; military cmmunications; and positioning, navigation, and timing systems used for weapons targeting. In addition, HELs could theoretically provide options for boost-phase missile intercept, given their speed-of-light travel time; however, experts disagree on the affordability, technological feasibility, and utility of this application. In general, HELs might offer lower costs per shot and— assuming access to a sufficient power supply—deeper magazines compared with traditional munitions. (Although a number of different types of HELs exist, many of the United States’ current programs are solid state lasers, which are fueled by electrical power. As a result, the cost per shot is equivalent to the cost of the electrical power required to fire the shot.) This could in turn produce a favorable cost exchange ratio for the defender, whose marginal costs would be significantly lower than those of the aggressor.

Monday, May 26, 2025
ROME -- Pope Leo XIV declared himself a Roman on Sunday as he completed the final ceremonial steps, cementing his role as the bishop of Rome.

The first American pope formally took possession of the St. John Lateran Basilica, which is Rome's cathedral and seat of the diocese, with an evening Mass attended by Roman priests and faithful.

He then took the popemobile for a visit to St. Mary Major, where he prayed before Pope Francis' tomb and an icon of the Virgin Mary beloved to many Roman faithful.

In his homily, Leo said he wanted to listen to them "in order to learn, understand and decide things together."

One of the many titles that Leo assumed when he was elected on May 8 was bishop of Rome. Given his responsibilities running the 1.4-billion strong universal Catholic Church, popes delegate the day-to-day governance of running of the diocese of Rome to a vicar.

Sunday's ceremonies at the St. John Lateran and a stop at St. Mary Major basilicas follow Leo's visit last week to the St. Paul Outside the Walls basilica. Together with St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican, the four papal basilicas are the most important basilicas in the West.

text:
🧬🔥 What if fat cells have a molecular brake that prevents them from burning stored lipids—and removing that brake could protect against obesity, insulin resistance, and fatty liver disease?

A new study in Cell Communication and Signaling identifies GDI2 as a negative regulator of adipocyte lipophagy and adaptive thermogenesis.

The central discovery:

GDI2 deletion → Rab7 activation → Autophagosome–lysosome fusion ↑ → Lipophagy ↑ → Free fatty acid release ↑ → PPARα–PGC1α–UCP1 signaling ↑ → Beige fat thermogenesis ↑

In mice, adipocyte-specific Gdi2 deletion increased energy expenditure and protected against high-fat diet-induced obesity, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and hepatic steatosis.

Importantly, the mechanism operates largely independently of canonical ATGL–HSL-mediated neutral lipolysis.

🔬 1. GDI2 emerges as an obesity-associated adipocyte regulator

GDP dissociation inhibitor 2 (GDI2) regulates intracellular membrane trafficking by controlling Rab-family small GTPases.

Rab proteins function as molecular switches governing vesicle trafficking, organelle interactions, and membrane fusion.

GDI2 typically binds GDP-associated Rab proteins and limits their membrane recruitment and activation.

The investigators found that GDI2 protein abundance increased during adipocyte differentiation.

Immunofluorescence and immunogold electron microscopy localized GDI2 to:

• Lipid droplet surfaces

• Endoplasmic reticulum–lipid droplet contact sites

• Cytoplasmic compartments

• Autolysosome-associated structures

These observations suggested that GDI2 might regulate intracellular lipid trafficking and degradation.

🧬 2. GDI2 expression increases in obesity but decreases during thermogenic activation

The researchers examined three mouse obesity models:

• Leptin-deficient ob/ob mice

• Leptin receptor-deficient db/db mice

• High-fat diet-induced obesity

GDI2 expression increased in inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT) and brown adipose tissue (BAT).

Its abundance was inversely associated with UCP1 expression.

Conversely, two thermogenic interventions reduced adipose GDI2 expression:

Cold exposure: 4 °C for 14 days

β3-adrenergic stimulation: CL316243 for 7 days

Human subcutaneous adipose tissue analyses provided supporting evidence.

Among 22 surgical patients, GDI2 mRNA correlated positively with BMI:

r = 0.6403

P = 0.0013

An independent dataset, GSE162653, also showed higher GDI2 expression in adipose tissue from individuals with obesity.

These findings associate GDI2 with adiposity, although the human evidence does not establish causality.

❄️ 3. Adipocyte-specific Gdi2 deletion enhances cold-induced thermogenesis

The investigators generated adipocyte-specific knockout mice:

Gdi2^flox/flox; Adipoq-Cre (Gdi2AKO)
At baseline, knockout mice exhibited no major differences in:

• Body weight

• Adipose tissue weight

• Circulating triglycerides

• Free fatty acids

• Glycerol

• Basal UCP1 abundance

However, following cold adaptation, the phenotype changed dramatically.

Gdi2AKO mice demonstrated:

Core body temperature ↑

Oxygen consumption ↑

Carbon dioxide production ↑

Heat production ↑

iWAT and eWAT mass ↓

Food intake and respiratory exchange ratio remained comparable between genotypes.

These findings indicate that Gdi2 deficiency increases thermogenic capacity during cold exposure rather than constitutively increasing basal energy expenditure.

🔥 4. The strongest thermogenic response occurs in inguinal white adipose tissue

Histological analysis revealed extensive remodeling of iWAT.

Control adipocytes predominantly contained large, unilocular lipid droplets.

Following cold exposure, Gdi2AKO adipocytes displayed:

• Smaller multilocular lipid droplets

• Increased UCP1-positive beige adipocytes

• Increased PGC1α expression

• Increased UCP1 protein abundance

Epididymal WAT showed a smaller but detectable browning response.

Interestingly, BAT showed no significant genotype-dependent increase in UCP1 abundance or lipid droplet remodeling.

GDI2 therefore appears particularly important for inducible WAT browning rather than further activation of classical brown fat.

⚡ 5. GDI2 deletion amplifies β3-adrenergic responses

To determine whether the phenotype depended specifically on cold exposure, researchers treated mice with the selective β3-adrenergic agonist CL316243.

Dose: 1 mg/kg/day

Duration: 7 days

Gdi2AKO mice exhibited:

• Greater cold tolerance

• Reduced WAT mass

• Increased multilocular adipocytes

• Increased UCP1 and PGC1α expression

• Increased circulating FFAs and glycerol

Ex vivo experiments using iWAT explants confirmed greater stimulated lipid release following:

CL316243: 1 μM

or

Forskolin: 10 μM

Basal lipid release remained similar.

This indicates that GDI2 limits stimulated lipid mobilization rather than simply determining basal lipid turnover.

🧪 6. The increased lipid mobilization is not explained by canonical neutral lipolysis

Adipocytes release fatty acids through two major pathways.

Neutral lipolysis

ATGL and HSL hydrolyze triglycerides through cytosolic enzymatic reactions.

Lipophagy

Lipid droplets are delivered to lysosomes through autophagic pathways and degraded by lysosomal enzymes.

The investigators examined whether GDI2 regulates ATGL–HSL signaling.

Following Gdi2 deletion:

• ATGL protein abundance remained unchanged.

• HSL protein abundance remained unchanged.

• HSL phosphorylation was not significantly altered.

• CREB phosphorylation was not significantly altered.

Nevertheless, stimulated FFA and glycerol release increased.

This suggested that the additional lipid mobilization originated from another pathway.

The researchers identified lipophagy as the principal mechanism.

🧫 7. GDI2 deletion accelerates lipid droplet degradation through lipophagy

CRISPR–Cas9-mediated Gdi2 knockout was performed in C3H10T1/2-derived adipocytes.

Following CL316243 stimulation:

Lipid droplet size ↓

Total lipid droplet content ↓

FFA release ↑

Glycerol release ↑

LC3B–lipid droplet colocalization ↑

Autophagy-associated protein changes included:

P62 ↓

LC3B ↓

PLIN1 ↓

PLIN2 ↓

LAMP2 ↑

The combined findings were consistent with accelerated lipophagic degradation.

Importantly, decreased LC3B abundance alone does not prove increased autophagy.

The investigators therefore performed additional experiments to distinguish enhanced autophagic flux from impaired autophagosome formation.

🔋 8. GDI2 regulates late-stage autophagic degradation rather than initiation

The researchers compared three pharmacological inhibitors:

3-Methyladenine (3-MA)

Inhibits early autophagosome formation.

Chloroquine (CQ)

Disrupts lysosomal acidification and degradation.

Bafilomycin A1 (Baf A1)

Inhibits vacuolar H⁺-ATPase and late-stage autophagic processing.

The results were particularly informative.

3-MA did not reverse the characteristic decrease in lipophagy-associated substrates in Gdi2-deficient cells.

Chloroquine partially reversed the phenotype.

Bafilomycin A1 completely reversed the observed substrate depletion.

These findings implicated late-stage autophagic degradation.

The investigators also used tandem:

mCherry–EGFP–LC3B

to distinguish autophagosomes from acidic autolysosomes.

Gdi2 knockout increased red-only puncta and reduced the yellow-to-red puncta ratio.

The results support accelerated autophagosome maturation and autolysosomal flux.

🧬 9. Rab7 is the molecular switch downstream of GDI2

Rab7 is a small GTPase that regulates late endosomal trafficking and autophagosome–lysosome fusion.

Its activity depends on nucleotide state:

Rab7–GDP: Predominantly inactive

Rab7–GTP: Active membrane-associated signaling

The researchers demonstrated:

• Partial GDI2–Rab7 colocalization.

• GDI2–RAB7A association by co-immunoprecipitation.

• Increased GTP-bound Rab7 following Gdi2 deletion and β3-adrenergic stimulation.

• No corresponding change in total Rab7 abundance.

Thus, GDI2 restrains Rab7-dependent membrane trafficking.

When GDI2 is absent, stimulated adipocytes exhibit increased active Rab7 and accelerated autophagic processing.

🛡️ 10. Rab7 knockdown reverses the lipophagy phenotype

The investigators used siRNA to reduce Rab7 expression in Gdi2-deficient adipocytes.

This intervention reversed the enhanced degradation of lipophagy-associated substrates.

It also reduced the additional:

FFA release

and

Glycerol release

observed after β3-adrenergic stimulation.

These results provide functional evidence that Rab7 is necessary for the enhanced lipophagy associated with Gdi2 deficiency.

The proposed mechanism is:

GDI2 → Rab7 inhibition → Reduced autophagosome–lysosome fusion

Conversely:

GDI2 loss → Rab7–GTP ↑ → Autolysosomal lipid degradation ↑

However, GDI2 regulates multiple Rab proteins, so additional Rab-dependent mechanisms cannot be excluded.

🔬 11. Electron microscopy confirms increased autolysosomes and mitochondrial abundance

Transmission electron microscopy revealed striking ultrastructural changes.

In Gdi2-deficient adipocytes:

• Autolysosome-associated structures increased.

• Multilamellar degradative compartments accumulated.

• Lipid droplets became smaller.

• Mitochondrial abundance increased.

Cold-exposed knockout iWAT also contained autolysosomes with recognizable lipid droplet remnants.

These observations support increased lipophagic activity in vivo.

The simultaneous increase in mitochondrial abundance suggested that lipid mobilization was accompanied by greater oxidative capacity.

⚙️ 12. GDI2 deficiency increases mitochondrial respiration

The investigators measured oxygen consumption using Seahorse extracellular flux analysis.

Under basal conditions, Gdi2-deficient and control adipocytes exhibited comparable respiratory parameters.

Following CL316243 stimulation, knockout adipocytes demonstrated:

Basal respiration ↑

Maximal respiration ↑

ATP-linked oxygen consumption ↑

Proton leak ↑

The increased proton leak is particularly relevant because UCP1-dependent thermogenesis dissipates the mitochondrial proton gradient as heat.

However, the Seahorse measurements do not directly establish that the entire increase in proton leak is mediated by UCP1.

Together, the findings demonstrate that Gdi2 deletion enhances mitochondrial oxidative capacity during thermogenic stimulation.

🧠 13. Transcriptomics identifies a coordinated thermogenic program

RNA sequencing was performed on iWAT from cold-exposed knockout and control mice.

The analysis identified:

188 upregulated genes

391 downregulated genes

Enriched pathways included:

• Thermogenesis

• Oxidative phosphorylation

• PPAR signaling

Key upregulated thermogenic genes included:

Ucp1

Dio2

Cidea

Cox7a1

Cox8b

Ucp3

Oxidative metabolism-associated genes included:

Cpt1b

Ndufa12

Ppargc1a

mt-Co1

mt-Co2

PPAR-associated genes included:

Ppara

Slc27a2

In contrast, major adipocyte differentiation markers were largely unchanged.

This suggests that Gdi2 deficiency enhances the thermogenic program without broadly disrupting mature adipocyte identity.

🔥 14. PPARα links lipophagy-derived fatty acids to thermogenic gene expression

Free fatty acids have two major roles in thermogenic adipocytes.

Metabolic substrates

They enter mitochondria and support fatty acid β-oxidation.

Signaling molecules

They activate lipid-sensitive nuclear receptors, including PPARα.

The investigators proposed that increased lipophagy-derived FFAs activate PPARα-dependent transcription.

Consistent with this hypothesis, Gdi2-deficient adipocytes exhibited increased:

PPARα

PGC1α

UCP1

The researchers then used the PPARα antagonist:

GW6471, 10 μM

This markedly attenuated the increase in thermogenic protein expression.

Rab7 knockdown produced a similar suppression.

These findings support a functional signaling sequence:

Rab7-dependent lipophagy → FFA availability → PPARα-associated transcription → Thermogenic gene expression

The study did not directly quantify PPARα ligand occupancy by individual lipophagy-derived fatty acid species.

🫀 15. GDI2 deletion protects against diet-induced obesity

The investigators fed male mice a high-fat diet containing:

60% of calories from fat

for:

16 weeks

Gdi2AKO mice began gaining significantly less weight from approximately week seven.

At the end of the intervention, knockout mice exhibited:

• Lower body weight

• Reduced adipose tissue mass

• Smaller adipocytes

• Increased energy expenditure

• Increased oxygen consumption

• Increased carbon dioxide production

• Increased heat production

Food intake and respiratory exchange ratio remained similar between genotypes.

These findings suggest that resistance to diet-induced obesity was associated with increased energy expenditure rather than reduced food consumption.

🩺 16. Metabolic protection extends beyond body weight

After 16 weeks of high-fat feeding, Gdi2AKO mice demonstrated:

Fasting triglycerides ↓

Total cholesterol ↓

Fasting glucose ↓

Serum ALT ↓

Circulating FFAs ↑

Glucose tolerance testing revealed improved glucose clearance.

Insulin tolerance testing showed greater insulin responsiveness.

Adipose tissue also exhibited reduced F4/80-positive macrophage infiltration.

These findings indicate that increased lipophagy and thermogenesis were associated with improved systemic metabolic regulation.

Importantly, the increase in circulating FFAs did not coincide with worsening insulin resistance in this model.

This suggests that enhanced lipid mobilization was accompanied by sufficient oxidative capacity to avoid the metabolic deterioration often associated with excessive fatty acid exposure.

🧬 17. GDI2 deletion also alleviates hepatic steatosis

The investigators examined liver outcomes after high-fat feeding.

Although Gdi2 deletion was restricted to adipocytes, knockout mice exhibited:

• Reduced liver weight

• Lower hepatic lipid accumulation

• Improved circulating metabolic markers

• Lower serum ALT

The authors proposed that hepatic protection resulted secondarily from increased adipose thermogenesis and improved systemic lipid metabolism.

This interpretation is plausible because Gdi2 was not directly deleted in hepatocytes.

However, the study did not perform detailed interorgan metabolic flux experiments to establish the precise mechanism of liver protection.

Therefore, the liver phenotype should be interpreted as an indirect systemic benefit associated with adipocyte Gdi2 deletion.

🎯 18. Integrated mechanism: GDI2 determines whether stored fat remains stored or supports thermogenesis

Normal GDI2 activity

Cold exposure / β3-adrenergic stimulation
↓
GDI2 retains Rab7 in an inactive state
↓
Rab7-dependent membrane fusion restricted
↓
Autophagosome–lysosome fusion limited
↓
Lipophagic lipid droplet degradation restrained
↓
FFA availability limited
↓
PPARα-dependent thermogenic signaling restrained
↓
Lower beige adipocyte thermogenic response

GDI2 deficiency
Cold exposure / β3-adrenergic stimulation
↓
Rab7–GTP activation ↑
↓
Autophagosome–lysosome fusion ↑
↓
Lipophagic degradation of lipid droplets ↑
↓
Free fatty acid availability ↑
↓
Two complementary processes:
A. Metabolic fuel
FFA → Mitochondrial β-oxidation → Energy supply for thermogenesis
B. Transcriptional activation
FFA → PPARα → PGC1α-associated thermogenic program → UCP1 expression ↑
Combined outcome:
Mitochondrial oxidative metabolism ↑
Thermogenic capacity ↑
Energy expenditure ↑
Resistance to diet-induced obesity and metabolic dysfunction
This mechanism highlights lipophagy as an active regulator of energy expenditure rather than merely a lipid droplet degradation pathway.
💊 19. Therapeutic implications
The study suggests several potential intervention strategies.
Adipocyte-selective GDI2 inhibition

Reducing GDI2 activity might enhance thermogenic responsiveness by releasing Rab7-dependent lipophagy.

Rab7-associated membrane trafficking
Modulating late-stage autophagic fusion may increase lipid mobilization during thermogenic stimulation.
Lipophagy–PPARα coupling
Enhancing the conversion of stored lipid into thermogenic signaling could potentially improve adipose metabolic function.
Beige fat activation
Targeting intracellular lipid degradation may complement β-adrenergic thermogenic stimulation.
Obesity-associated fatty liver
Increasing adipose energy expenditure may indirectly reduce hepatic lipid accumulation.
However, these strategies remain preclinical.
No selective GDI2 inhibitor was tested for obesity treatment in vivo.
Furthermore, GDI2 regulates multiple Rab proteins and participates in membrane trafficking across several cell types.

Systemic inhibition could therefore produce unintended effects.

🚨 20. Critical limitations

• All animal experiments used male mice.

• The study did not establish whether female mice exhibit comparable responses.

• The knockout model used constitutive Adipoq-Cre rather than inducible deletion in adult animals.

• Developmental effects cannot be completely excluded.

• GDI2 regulates multiple Rab GTPases, not only Rab7.

• The complete downstream Rab interaction network was not characterized.

• The relative contributions of iWAT and BAT require additional tissue-specific models.

• The human analysis involved a small observational cohort of 22 participants.

• No human adipocyte-specific GDI2 loss-of-function experiment demonstrated enhanced thermogenesis.

• No pharmacological GDI2 inhibitor was evaluated in obese mice.

• The study did not directly quantify fatty acid flux from lipophagy into mitochondrial β-oxidation.

• Individual fatty acid species activating PPARα were not identified.

• The direct contribution of UCP1 to the increased whole-body energy expenditure was not established using Ucp1-deficient mice.

• The long-term consequences of sustained lipophagy activation were not evaluated.

• The study did not establish whether GDI2 inhibition reverses established obesity.

• Human clinical efficacy and safety remain unknown.

An important translational consideration is that increasing lipophagy without a corresponding increase in fatty acid oxidation could potentially cause lipid redistribution or metabolic stress.

Therefore, therapeutic strategies would need to preserve coupling between lipid mobilization and energy dissipation.

💡 Key takeaway

Fat storage and thermogenesis are linked by a Rab7-dependent lysosomal lipid degradation pathway controlled by GDI2.

This study identifies GDI2 as a molecular brake on adipocyte lipophagy.

Removing GDI2 increases Rab7-dependent autophagosome–lysosome fusion, accelerates lipid droplet degradation, and increases free fatty acid availability.

These fatty acids support mitochondrial oxidation and activate a PPARα-associated thermogenic transcriptional program.

In male mice, this mechanism enhances beige fat thermogenesis and protects against diet-induced obesity, insulin resistance, and hepatic steatosis.

The broader conceptual advance is:

Rab-dependent membrane trafficking ↔ Lipophagy ↔ Lipid signaling ↔ Mitochondrial thermogenesis ↔ Systemic metabolic health

The findings suggest that selectively manipulating adipocyte lipid trafficking could offer a complementary strategy for increasing energy expenditure, although pharmacological feasibility and human relevance remain to be established.

📄 Gao F, Zhang Y, Liu D, et al.

Adipocyte GDI2 suppresses lipophagy to restrain adaptive thermogenesis and promotes diet-induced obesity.

Interesting…

EMINEM’S GREAT-GRANDFATHER & THE MAN WHO INITIATED ALEISTER CROWLEY

A man in a ritual mask and Highland dress turned up at 36 Blythe Road in Hammersmith in April 1900. Beneath the mask was Aleister Crowley, carrying written authority to take possession of the rooms used by the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. The man who sent him was Samuel Liddell “MacGregor” Mathers, the occultist whose name has since surfaced in a claim about Eminem’s great-grandfather.

Three months earlier, Crowley had crossed the Channel because the London members had refused to admit him to their inner circle. Mathers had helped found the Golden Dawn in 1888 and considered himself perfectly entitled to overrule them. In Paris, he personally conducted the initiation that his colleagues in London had refused to perform. Crowley returned to England owing his place in the Second Order to one man and in April that man called in the favour.

Waiting on the other side of the dispute was the Irish poet W. B. Yeats, a member of the same order who had little affection for Crowley. Yeats and fellow member Edmund Hunter took the matter straight to the landlord and demanded to know how Crowley had gained entry. The landlord sided with the London members, a constable intervened and the rooms slipped from Mathers’ control. Crowley would eventually fall out with his former mentor, but on that April morning he was prepared to take on the London membership for him.

Samuel’s own family had a bloodline story remarkable enough to explain why a man born in London answered to a Highland name and a French title. His wife Moina wrote that an ancestor named Ian MacGregor of Glenstrae fled to France after the Jacobite rising of 1745 and later fought at Pondicherry in India. According to her account, Louis XV made Ian the Comte de Glenstrae, a title Samuel himself used while living in France. Moina put the family account in the preface to her husband’s translation of The Kabbalah Unveiled, where anyone opening the book could read it.

Eminem’s family offers one detail easily missed in the story about his supposed occult great-grandfather. The rapper was born Marshall Bruce Mathers III, following a father and grandfather who both carried the same name. Go back one more generation and the name changes for the first time in that sequence. Independent genealogist William Addams Reitwiesner identifies that man as Chester William Mathers, born in Missouri in September 1885.

When Crowley appeared at Blythe Road on Samuel’s orders, Chester was 14 years old and living an entirely different chapter of the Mathers story. In 1915, Chester became the father of the first Marshall Bruce Mathers, whose son would later give the name to Eminem. Samuel died in Paris in 1918, more than half a century before the rapper was born. Chester lived until January 1972, missing the birth of his great-grandson by just nine months.

text:
Octogon house. There were several. There was one in my husband's home town in Wisconsin. "Octagon houses are eight-sided residential structures that emerged as a distinctive architectural style in the United States during the mid-19th century, largely popularized by phrenologist Orson Squire Fowler through his 1848 book A Home for All.  Fowler argued that the octagonal shape offered superior ventilation, natural light, heat retention, and structural stability compared to rectangular homes, leading to the construction of several thousand such houses primarily between 1850 and 1870.

Notable surviving examples include the Armour-Stiner House in Irvington, New York, which is the only known fully domed octagonal residence in the country, and Longwood in Natchez, Mississippi, the largest octagon house in the United States, which remains unfinished after construction halted during the Civil War.  Other significant historic structures include the Octagon House in Washington, D.C., built in 1799 and used by President James Madison, and the McElroy Octagon House in San Francisco, a concrete "gravel wall" structure built in 1861 that now serves as a museum.

While the craze was short-lived, many of these homes have been preserved as historic landmarks. Current listings indicate that while fewer than 100 original 19th-century octagonal houses remain, some are occasionally available for sale, such as a five-bedroom property in Colrain, Massachusetts, and an Italianate brick octagon in Monroeville, Ohio."

Closest approach occurs at 0350 UT on May 12, 2031 (142.1° Ls) with an apparent planetary disk diameter of 16.9 at a distance of 0.5533578 astronomical units (AU) or 51,437,823 miles (82,781,152 km). text:
Finally fully finished Cyberpunk 2077

My Thoughts;

A very fun and ambitious game that wanted to do so much more but couldn’t quite fully reach it’s full potential

The game is absolutely riddled with potential, you can feel exactly what they are going for with each individual mechanic but more often than not it ends up falling short of what it could have been

Story and Characters;

This game is not an RPG, at least not a good RPG, it is no Fallout or Elder Scrolls, your choices have minimal impact on the story and only really effect the ending you go for

Phantom Liberty partially fixes this with it’s own DLC story, but even then it’s not a proper fix to the innate issues of the game

The characters are so good, I love their stories and personalities, the main story is amazing and I wish it wasn’t so deceptively short

I am a very sentimental person and I often find myself becoming melancholic because I exhausted a central character’s purpose in the game, and now all they have to offer is the same static responses being repeated endlessly, I love their presence and all I want to do is interact with them more

I actually found myself becoming misty eyed at times, particularly with Jackie and his family, and I think the biggest mistake the game made was having Jackie die at the very beginning and having his presence be made minimal in the overarching story as a result

I was extremely disappointed by how little you can actually interact with any major characters, CDPR tried to make up for this by adding dates you can go on with your romantic partner, but even this falls short of what it could be and there is no purpose in doing so beyond the first time, you don’t unlock any new interactions

(My favorite character is Misty 💜)

Gameplay;

The combat is fun, but even when playing on hard the game was simply not very difficult at all, the power fantasy was nice but after awhile it becomes boring, and from what I have read the ‘very hard’ difficulty just makes the enemies tankier, which is lame

Enemy AI leaves a lot to be desired, enemy variety doesn’t really exist, the only actual enemy categories are human and machine, both of which act universally identical in their respective categories

Occasionally you’ll find an enemy that is somewhat of a challenge, usually because they auto dodge all your attacks, and that’s about as advanced as it gets in terms of enemy difficulty

The world is a treat to explore, Night City always had something new around every corner, whether it be a crime scene, side quest or a hidden area, it was always fun to stumble upon a new hidden weapon or badass vehicle to add to your arsenal (my favorite car is the Riptide Terrier)

I feel whelmed by the perk trees, there’s lots of cool stuff but a lot of it is bogged down by odd design choices, also apparently like 50% of the perks are either broken or just flat out wrong about what they do

Your presence in the game never really grows, V never becomes a legend or renowned, characters never really show you any respect despite knowing what you are capable of, and that kind of hinders the power fantasy a bit

Gunplay is fine, Netrunning is cool but boring, stealth mechanics are okay, cyberwear is awesome but could definitely be better

The worst part about the game BY FAR is the character customization because holy shit it’s so bad, why is it so bad???

Conclusion;

8/10

Sadly I have little faith in the sequel, with CDPR drinking a whole punch bowl of DEI ESG Koolaid, I just don’t trust them to not ruin a sequel with modern political drivel

This was present in 2077, but it was at least somewhat tolerable (Claire is awful though), so I pray I’m wrong about Orion or whatever the sequel will be called

You can feel the TTRPG influence and I hope the sequel has much more of this present

text:
Mathematics and Elite Squad Dynamics
A Modest Proposal for the Improvement of American Civilization Through Grand Theft Auto VI
Being an earnest inquiry into the moral, economic, and technological benefits of spending thirteen years constructing a virtual Florida in which Americans may commit the crimes they are too exhausted to commit in the actual one.

November 19, 2026 — Launch Day

By our Special Correspondent for Applied Degeneracy, Digital Economics, and the Collapse of Western Civilization

It is with considerable satisfaction that I announce the arrival of Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest triumph of American ingenuity, in which a civilization possessing the means to simulate entire metropolitan areas has elected to devote those means to stealing automobiles, shooting policemen, and purchasing trousers.

The enterprise has consumed thirteen years.

This is approximately the length of time required to educate a physician, establish a successful agricultural cooperative, or bring a moderately incompetent infrastructure project to its second environmental-impact assessment.

Rockstar Games, however, has employed this period to achieve something arguably more ambitious: Florida, but with functioning collision detection.

I consider this a remarkable accomplishment, particularly as the original Florida has thus far resisted such an improvement.
I. Concerning the Present Scarcity of Meaningful Employment
There are, by some accounts, millions of young men in the United States who feel alienated from the economy, isolated from society, and disenchanted with the promises of capitalism.

Fortunately, an international consortium of computer programmers has found an answer.

They shall become car thieves.

Not actual car thieves, of course, for that would inconvenience the insurance industry and occasion considerable police attention. Rather, they shall purchase expensive computing equipment, subscribe to high-speed internet services, and engage in imaginary car theft under conditions carefully negotiated by corporate lawyers.

They shall experience liberty.

They shall experience rebellion.

They shall experience the exhilarating freedom of driving a stolen Lamborghini directly into a municipal fountain, after which they shall purchase a new pair of virtual sunglasses.

And what better emblem of the modern American spirit could there be than a man who has spent eighty dollars for permission to disobey laws that do not exist?

The criminal of the eighteenth century had at least the satisfaction of depriving a wealthy gentleman of his property.

The criminal of the twenty-first century must first purchase his own copy of the wealthy gentleman's property, agree to its terms of service, and occasionally download an update.

Thus has capitalism accomplished what two centuries of law enforcement could not: it has made robbery profitable for the person being robbed.
II. A Wonderful New Species of Rebellion
I am particularly delighted by the philosophical sophistication of the enterprise.

The game is a satire of American consumer culture, financed by an enormously successful corporation, distributed through multinational technology platforms, and marketed through one of the most extravagant exercises in consumer anticipation ever devised.

It condemns materialism.

It offers an Ultimate Edition.

It mocks our obsession with brands.

It has a merchandise store.

It exposes the hollow promises of consumer capitalism.

It would be grateful if you subscribed.

I cannot imagine a more perfect arrangement. Indeed, I propose that the Smithsonian immediately establish a permanent exhibition dedicated to the subject, entitled:

THE REVOLUTION WILL BE MONETIZED.

Admission: $79.99.

Gift-shop access requires the Ultimate Edition.
III. Of the Peculiar Customs of the People of Leonida
The fictional state of Leonida, we are assured, bears a striking resemblance to Florida.

I have examined this proposition with considerable care.

Leonida contains criminals, swamps, alligators, aspiring celebrities, extravagant wealth, conspiratorial thinking, astonishingly poor judgment, and people who regard the operation of motor vehicles as a competitive contact sport.

Florida contains these things also.

The principal distinction appears to be that in Leonida, a computer must labor intensely to produce such phenomena, whereas in Florida they arise spontaneously from the interaction of sunlight, alcohol, and municipal zoning regulations.

This suggests a fascinating scientific question.

If a simulation becomes sufficiently faithful to Florida, does it eventually develop its own homeowners' association?

And if so, can the association be defeated with a rocket launcher?

I submit this as a suitable subject for doctoral research.

The developers have reportedly constructed an enormous world of beaches, highways, neighborhoods, businesses, wildlife, weather, and intricate human behavior.

Here is an opportunity for unprecedented artistic achievement.

The human player may encounter the complexity of an entire civilization.

He may examine its inequalities, confront its moral contradictions, explore its architecture, and investigate the subtle interplay between personal freedom and institutional power.

Or he may hit a pedestrian with a golf cart.

I predict the latter will receive considerable scholarly attention.
IV. Concerning Two Young Persons of Questionable Character
Our protagonists are Jason and Lucia, two young people seeking prosperity in a society whose economic opportunities have largely been monopolized by persons already possessing prosperity.

They are, in other words, entrepreneurs.

Their business model differs from that of Silicon Valley principally in that their thefts are represented directly on the screen.

A venture capitalist might observe that the pair have a compelling founding story, strong execution capability, excellent geographical market penetration, and an unusually aggressive customer-acquisition strategy.

Their principal deficiency is that they have not yet described their enterprise as artificial intelligence.

This may be remedied.

I propose a startup called CrimeGPT, whose purpose is to automate the commission of virtual felonies, thereby liberating the player to pursue higher-order activities such as reading quarterly shareholder reports.

Its seed round shall be $400 million.

Its product shall be an animated button labeled STEAL CAR.

Its founders shall describe it as transformational.

They will not be wrong.
V. An Inquiry Into the Extraordinary Patience of the Gaming Public
Thirteen years.

Permit me to dwell upon this figure.

Thirteen years is an age at which a child may begin to develop independent moral reasoning.

A child born on the release date of Grand Theft Auto V is now old enough to ask why his father has spent the greater part of his adult life awaiting its sequel.

The father will explain that the new game possesses more realistic reflections, improved pedestrian behavior, and substantially greater fidelity in the depiction of automotive upholstery.

The child will naturally ask whether these advances have improved civilization.

The father will say that he does not know, but that the water looks absolutely incredible.

And it does.

We have reached the extraordinary stage of technical progress at which a simulated puddle may require more computational effort than the entire Apollo guidance computer, while serving the equally noble purpose of reflecting the undercarriage of a stolen pickup truck.

I shall not criticize this allocation of resources.

I merely suggest that NASA should have considered giving Neil Armstrong a wanted level.
VI. The Internet, Having Finally Met Its Natural Enemy
Today, November 19, 2026, the game has arrived.

According to contemporary reporting, its download is approximately 212 gigabytes.
AP News+1

This is a remarkable quantity of information to transmit for the purpose of enabling a man to drive badly.

Internet providers have been obliged to prepare for the consequent demand.

Somewhere, at this very moment, a network engineer is gazing at a wall of flashing equipment and contemplating the civilization that has entrusted him with its infrastructure.

He has studied mathematics.

He has studied telecommunications.

He understands packet switching, congestion control, redundancy, and the statistical properties of network traffic.

He knows that the internet might facilitate universal education, international scientific cooperation, and the free exchange of human knowledge.

Instead, seven hundred thousand men are simultaneously attempting to download the same simulated strip club.

The engineer reaches for his coffee.

The router begins blinking.

And so, perhaps, does God.
VII. A Few Words Concerning the Moral Improvement of Youth
Critics of the franchise have long argued that games of this nature encourage antisocial behavior.

This criticism, though doubtless sincere, seems to overlook the remarkable degree of social discipline required to participate in the modern gaming economy.

The average customer must:
Obey the platform's rules.
Maintain an account in good standing.
Accept the publisher's licensing conditions.
Preserve sufficient disk space.
Remain connected to the relevant services where required.
Refrain from certain prohibited forms of misconduct.
Having fulfilled these obligations, he may then enjoy the thrilling fantasy of being an individual who refuses to obey rules.

Thus, the modern criminal imagination is now cultivated in a carefully regulated commercial environment.

It is as though Robin Hood had been required to enroll in a loyalty program before entering Sherwood Forest.

There are rewards.

There are incentives.

There may be exclusive seasonal benefits.

The outlaw has become an account holder.

The revolution has a customer-support department.
VIII. The Great Philosophical Discovery
There is, however, one feature of this phenomenon that troubles me deeply.

For decades, artists, philosophers, educators, and political reformers have struggled to persuade the public to examine the absurdities of modern American life.

They have written books.

They have produced documentaries.

They have organized demonstrations.

They have delivered lectures upon the moral bankruptcy of consumerism, the corrupting influence of wealth, the theatrical nature of celebrity, and the increasing difficulty of distinguishing public life from commercial entertainment.

Most have been ignored.

Rockstar Games has discovered a superior method.

It has constructed a colossal satire of the very same society, placed a stolen automobile in the foreground, and sold tickets to the experience.

Millions have arrived.

This represents a devastating indictment of the literary profession.

Jonathan Swift spent years fashioning arguments of exquisite irony and moral precision.

He might have achieved vastly greater commercial success had he included a minimap and a button for punching horses.

Indeed, A Modest Proposal itself might have enjoyed an altogether different reception under the title:

GRAND THEFT IRELAND: THE POTATO HEIST.

Downloadable content: The Landlord Expansion.
IX. My Own Modest Proposal
Having considered the matter, I believe the franchise has not yet gone far enough.

Its developers should cease representing American society through satire and instead reproduce the institutions of American life with absolute fidelity.

I therefore recommend the following features for Grand Theft Auto VII.

The player shall begin with $47,000 in student debt.

His principal antagonist shall be a health-insurance company.

The wanted-level system shall be replaced by a credit score.

Successful criminal enterprises shall obtain venture financing, become too large to fail, and acquire their competitors.

The final mission shall involve navigating a customer-service telephone tree.

A player wishing to purchase property shall be required to demonstrate three years of stable income and provide documentation of previous rental history.

Police pursuit shall be suspended whenever the player enters a sufficiently expensive neighborhood.

The protagonist's automobile shall depreciate immediately upon purchase.

The player shall be unable to progress to the next mission until a state agency processes his application.

And the ultimate achievement, accessible only after approximately 400 hours of play, shall be called:

HOMEOWNERSHIP.

Upon unlocking it, the player shall receive a notification that his property taxes have increased.

This, I submit, would be a truly adult video game.
X. A Final Consideration of the Human Condition
The genius of Grand Theft Auto is not that it allows its players to escape the world.

It is that it persuades them to purchase a second world that is even more ridiculous than the first, while congratulating themselves on having recognized the ridiculousness.

There is something almost tender about this arrangement.

We have built machines capable of calculating the motions of galaxies, modeling molecular interactions, and examining the most delicate structures of mathematical logic.

We connect them across a planetary communications network whose existence would have seemed supernatural to nearly every human being who ever lived.

And what do we do?

We simulate Florida.

Not because we are obliged to.

Not because Florida is in danger of extinction.

Not because the real Florida has become inaccessible, although this possibility cannot be entirely dismissed.

We do it because the simulated Florida permits us to commit atrocities without consequence, acquire wealth without labor, and inhabit a world where the moral bankruptcy of society is at least accompanied by an excellent soundtrack.

And we call it entertainment.

I cannot say whether this represents the pinnacle of human civilization or the moment at which civilization quietly excused itself from the room.

But I am inclined to believe that future archaeologists, examining the surviving data centers of our age, will conclude that we worshipped a peculiar deity called Rockstar, who appeared once every thirteen years, demanded considerable tribute, and rewarded the faithful with increasingly realistic representations of asphalt.

They will marvel at our ingenuity.

They will mourn our priorities.

And somewhere in the ruins, a server will still be attempting to verify a license.

Editorial conclusion
It is difficult to remain entirely pessimistic.

For all its absurdities, humanity has finally achieved something philosophers have sought since antiquity:

A world in which crime pays, death is temporary, and the laws of physics can be defeated by driving a motorcycle up a staircase.

The price of admission is reasonable, provided one does not count the console, the broadband service, the additional storage, the electricity, the optional premium benefits, and the thirteen years of one's mortal existence spent waiting.

We may therefore proclaim with confidence that the future has arrived.

It is beautiful.

It is grotesque.

It is available for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
And the internet is blinking.

God help us all.

Mathematics and Elite Squad Dynamics

All bullshit is welcome. Unlabeled bullshit is not.

Editorial disclosure: This is satire, not a gameplay review. The release date, setting, characters, and launch details are grounded in Rockstar's November 19 announcement and official game materials. The proposed features, institutions, and philosophical diagnoses are products of the author's increasingly reasonable despair.

text:
Always a rowdy discussion with students about this paragraph, which I think is one of the greatest paragraphs ever composed in theological literature…

“God from all eternity did, by the most wise and holy counsel of his own will, freely and unchangeably ordain whatsoever comes to pass; yet so as thereby neither is God the author of sin, nor is violence offered to the will of the creatures, nor is the liberty or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established.” (WCF, Ch 3)

Today, this is where our discussion went…

When you’re reading a book that is written in third person omniscient, you are being led along from scene to scene by a narrator who knows everything there is to know about the story. You don’t know everything there is to know as the reader, but with the third person narration, the author himself is revealing the story to you, and once you get to the end, you will share his omniscience of the story.

When we approach the deep things of God, when we come up to, say, the mystery of God’s absolute sovereignty and human responsibility, we are prone to expect the third person omniscient narrative to kick in. We are prone to think, “If I just keep asking question after question, eventually I’ll understand this and it’ll all make sense.”

But the problem is, we are less like readers of a book, and more like characters in a book. 

A theology student trying to get to the bottom of the sovereignty of God in relationship to his own free will would be like Huck Finn having a conversation with Jim on their raft questioning why Mark Twain wrote his dad into the story as a drunk.

And while that does kind of sound like a scene that Mark Twain might’ve come up with, nothing like that occurs in the book because Twain preserves the suspension of disbelief for his readers.

That’s exactly the thing we need more of as students of God… 

The suspension of disbelief.

In our pride, we look at divine transcendence and are quick to doubt and question based on our inability to comprehend. In short, in our pride we are quick to disbelieve, as if our not believing actually alters reality.

And this is the very thing we should be more quick to suspend. 

To, in humility, kneel under the immensity of the God who is exhaustively sovereign, and suspend our disbelief.

The Council of Clermont was a mixed synod of ecclesiastics and laymen of the Catholic Church, called by Pope Urban II and held from 17 to 27 November 1095 at Clermont, Auvergne, at the time part of the Duchy of Aquitaine.[1][2]

While the council is known today primarily for the speech Pope Urban gave on the final day, it was primarily a synod focused on implementing the Cluniac reforms, enacting decrees and settling local and regional issues.[3] This also included the extension of the excommunication of Philip I of France for his adulterous remarriage to Bertrade of Montfort and a declaration of renewal of the Truce of God, an attempt on the part of the church to reduce feuding among Frankish nobles.[4]

Pope Urban's speech on 27 November included the call to arms that would result in the First Crusade,[5] and eventually the capture of Jerusalem and the establishment of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. In this, Urban reacted to the request by Byzantine emperor Alexius I Comnenus who had sent envoys to the Council of Piacenza requesting military assistance against the Seljuk Turks.[6] Several accounts of the speech survive; of these, the one by Fulcher of Chartres, who was present at the council, is generally accepted as the most reliable.

Evidence that the moral prohibition of homosexual practice remains in effect
The traditional Christian reading holds that same-sex sexual activity is contrary to God’s moral law, rooted in creation order and reaffirmed in the New Testament. This is distinct from temporary ceremonial regulations of the Mosaic covenant.
1. Rooted in creation, not merely Mosaic civil or ceremonial law.
Genesis 1–2 establishes the binary of male and female and the one-flesh union of marriage. Jesus reaffirms this as the creation pattern in Matthew 19:4–6 (“from the beginning… male and female… the two shall become one flesh”). Sexual ethics in the New Testament repeatedly appeal to this created order.
2. Old Testament prohibitions belong to the moral law.
Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13 prohibit a man lying with a man “as with a woman.” These stand in the same chapters as prohibitions of incest, adultery, and bestiality—acts treated as moral violations against the created order, not temporary ritual purity rules (contrast food laws or clothing mixtures). The surrounding context is the holiness required of God’s people because he is holy.
3. Explicit New Testament reaffirmation.
•  Romans 1:26–27: Paul describes both female and male same-sex relations as an “exchange” of “natural relations” for those “contrary to nature.” The argument is grounded in creation and the rejection of the Creator, not limited to pederasty, exploitation, or idolatrous temple rites. The language is mutual (“inflamed with lust for one another”).
•  1 Corinthians 6:9–11: The list of those who will not inherit the kingdom includes malakoi (“soft ones,” often the passive partner) and arsenokoitai (a term formed from the Greek of Leviticus 18:22 / 20:13, meaning men who lie with males). The list treats these alongside adultery, theft, greed, etc. The phrase “such were some of you” indicates that the behavior is incompatible with the kingdom yet changeable through washing, sanctification, and justification.
•  1 Timothy 1:9–10: Similar vice list includes those who practice homosexuality as contrary to sound doctrine and the law.
•  Jude 7: Sodom and Gomorrah are cited for “sexual immorality and perversion” / “going after strange flesh” as an example of judgment.
4. Continuity with Jesus’ teaching on the law.
Jesus’ statement in Matthew 5 that he came to fulfill rather than abolish, together with his intensification of moral demands and his affirmation of the male-female marriage pattern, provides no basis for discarding the sexual ethic of the Law and Prophets. The apostles, writing under his authority, continue that ethic for the church.
5. Distinction between categories of law.
Christian theology has long distinguished the moral law (reflecting God’s character and creation order, permanent), ceremonial law (fulfilled in Christ), and civil law (for ancient Israel’s theocracy). Sexual prohibitions in Leviticus 18/20 and their New Testament counterparts fall into the moral category. The New Testament treats sexual immorality (including same-sex acts) as still forbidden for believers.
This has been the historic consensus of the Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions. Revisionist interpretations exist that limit the texts to specific cultural abuses or re-read “nature,” but they require departing from the plain sense of the language, the creation grounding, and the consistent trajectory of both Testaments. The same texts that prohibit the practice also announce that those who turn from it can be washed, sanctified, and justified (1 Corinthians 6:11). The moral standard remains; the offer of grace is universal.

While it is well known that Krishnadevaraya’s celebrated Telugu Kavya, Amuktamalyada, narrates the life and devotion of Sri Andal, another significant aspect of Tamilakam’s Vaishnava tradition finds a beautiful place in this literary masterpiece. The Kaisika Mahatmyam, associated with the sacred shrine of Tirukkurungudi near Tirunelveli, is elaborately retold by Krishnadevaraya as the Maladasari Katha.

In this episode, a Brahmarakshasa intercepts Nampaduvan, a Panan (singer) and an ardent devotee of Mahavishnu, who is on his way to worship at Tirukkurungudi. Nampaduvan promises to return and offer himself to the Brahmarakshasa after completing his musical worship of Perumal. Though initially reluctant, the Brahmarakshasa eventually lets him proceed.

Having rendered his devotional songs in the Kaisika Pann, Nampaduvan returns to fulfil his promise, even when Perumal himself, appearing in disguise, advises him to take an alternative route. Unwilling to compromise his adherence to Dharma, Nampaduvan remains steadfast in his resolve. Deeply moved by his devotion and truthfulness, the Brahmarakshasa seeks redemption by requesting a share of the spiritual merit earned through his musical worship. Nampaduvan grants his request, thereby liberating him from his curse.

This sacred narrative continues to be enacted as Kaisika Natakam at the Tirukkurungudi temple on the auspicious occasion of Kaisika Ekadasi, which is celebrated today

What is particularly remarkable is that a deeply rooted Vaishnava tradition associated with a temple in the far south of Tamilakam finds such an elaborate expression in the Telugu Kavya of a Vijayanagara emperor. It reflects the profound understanding and appreciation that Krishnadevaraya had of the religious and cultural traditions of Tamilakam.

Beyond its literary brilliance, Amuktamalyada stands as a magnificent testimony to the underlying civilisational unity of Bharat, where linguistic and geographical boundaries never stood in the way of a shared spiritual and cultural heritage.

The Council of Clermont was a mixed synod of ecclesiastics and laymen of the Catholic Church, called by Pope Urban II and held from 17 to 27 November 1095 at Clermont, Auvergne, at the time part of the Duchy of Aquitaine.[1][2]

While the council is known today primarily for the speech Pope Urban gave on the final day, it was primarily a synod focused on implementing the Cluniac reforms, enacting decrees and settling local and regional issues.[3] This also included the extension of the excommunication of Philip I of France for his adulterous remarriage to Bertrade of Montfort and a declaration of renewal of the Truce of God, an attempt on the part of the church to reduce feuding among Frankish nobles.[4]

Pope Urban's speech on 27 November included the call to arms that would result in the First Crusade,[5] and eventually the capture of Jerusalem and the establishment of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. In this, Urban reacted to the request by Byzantine emperor Alexius I Comnenus who had sent envoys to the Council of Piacenza requesting military assistance against the Seljuk Turks.[6] Several accounts of the speech survive; of these, the one by Fulcher of Chartres, who was present at the council, is generally accepted as the most reliable.

Once the State of Israel was born, the fate of Jerusalem and the holy places continued to be an issue of Vatican concern, together with the evolution of the Arab-Israeli conflict, the fate of Christian communities in the Middle East, and the question of recognition or non-recognition of the new state. As Vatican expert Henry Bocala pointed out, the Holy See viewed the question of Jerusalem as a religious issue (protection of the holy places) with a political dimension (the legal status of the city). Here, Rome saw itself as a party to the dispute and, consequently, not only asked for a resolution but also demanded a say over the outcome. Initially, it asked for the internationalization of Jerusalem and the holy places, and from 1967 onwards modified its position in pursuit of an internationally guaranteed special status. The Arab-Israeli conflict was seen as a political problem (a clash between two nationalisms) with a religious component (the diminished Christian presence in the Holy Land). Here, Rome saw itself in the role of a conciliator and asked for a resolution without proposing details for it.3

This did not prevent the Papacy from adopting a pro-Palestinian position. The Holy See propagated the idea that the Palestinians were the main victims of the conflict, that the Israelis were responsible for their condition, as well as the notion that without a solution to their cause there could be no peace in the region. Rome’s stand on the Arab-Israeli conflict was reflected in this phrase by the President of the Pontifical Mission for Palestine, Monsignor John Nolan: “If the Palestinians have no voice, we are their voice.”4

Rome’s endorsement of Palestinian national aspirations did not echo its lack of support for Jewish national yearnings before 1948, and once the Jewish state was established it took the Vatican decades to establish diplomatic ties. An Israeli official based in Rome expressed Jerusalem’s annoyance thus: “Our position was clear: we are always ready. If you truly wish to normalize relations, you have only to say the word. Our address is the same as it was 2,000 years ago.”5

As the first Israeli ambassador to the Holy See, the late Shmuel Hadas, observed, early recognition of Israel could have been a historic opportunity for the Catholic Church to rectify – albeit partially – its past hostility toward Jews and its silence during the Holocaust.6 Rome chose to see things in a different way. Only after the PLO agreed to formally recognize Israel in September 1993 did the Holy See decide to do the same, two months later. By then, the State of Israel had lived through forty-five years of sovereign life.

In December 1993, the Fundamental Agreement was signed between the parties and in June 1994, Israel and the Holy See exchanged ambassadors. A new horizon in relations between the two emerged, and the bond between Rome and Jerusalem was finally normalized.

The Council of Clermont was a mixed synod of ecclesiastics and laymen of the Catholic Church, called by Pope Urban II and held from 17 to 27 November 1095 at Clermont, Auvergne, at the time part of the Duchy of Aquitaine.[1][2]

While the council is known today primarily for the speech Pope Urban gave on the final day, it was primarily a synod focused on implementing the Cluniac reforms, enacting decrees and settling local and regional issues.[3] This also included the extension of the excommunication of Philip I of France for his adulterous remarriage to Bertrade of Montfort and a declaration of renewal of the Truce of God, an attempt on the part of the church to reduce feuding among Frankish nobles.[4]

Pope Urban's speech on 27 November included the call to arms that would result in the First Crusade,[5] and eventually the capture of Jerusalem and the establishment of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. In this, Urban reacted to the request by Byzantine emperor Alexius I Comnenus who had sent envoys to the Council of Piacenza requesting military assistance against the Seljuk Turks.[6] Several accounts of the speech survive; of these, the one by Fulcher of Chartres, who was present at the council, is generally accepted as the most reliable.

Britain's 1939 White Paper capped Jewish immigration at 75,000 over 5 years, as Jews fled the Holocaust. And ~850,000 Jews were driven from Arab lands after 1948; their descendants are a large share of Israelis. Not 'white colonists.' Insults aren't an argument.

The land was never a sovereign Palestinian Arab state. For centuries it was Ottoman territory (an empire that collapsed in World War I). The 1922 League of Nations Mandate for Palestine explicitly recognized the historical connection of the Jewish people to the territory and provided for a Jewish national home while protecting the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities. 

At the time of the Mandate, the area contained a Jewish population with continuous presence dating back millennia (kingdoms of Israel and Judah, Second Temple period, and ongoing communities) alongside an Arab majority that had grown under Ottoman rule through natural increase and migration. Neither group held exclusive title in the modern sense of a nation-state. 

In 1947 the UN General Assembly passed Resolution 181 partitioning the Mandate into a Jewish state and an Arab state. The Jewish leadership accepted it; the Arab leadership and neighboring Arab states rejected it and launched war. Israel declared independence in 1948, was recognized by the United States and others, and was admitted to the UN in 1949. That is the same legal pathway used by many post-imperial states. 

The subsequent Arab-Israeli wars, refugee flows in both directions (roughly 700,000 Arabs left or were expelled; roughly 800,000 Jews were expelled from Arab countries), and armistice lines did not erase the original partition decision or the prior Jewish legal claim under the Mandate. Claims that Israel is uniquely illegitimate because it sits on “Palestinian land” usually rely on one of two assertions that do not hold under scrutiny: (1) that demographic majority at a particular moment in the early 20th century confers exclusive permanent title, or (2) that Jewish return and statehood after the Holocaust and centuries of diaspora is somehow more illegitimate than other post-imperial partitions and population movements. 

Both standards, if applied consistently, would dissolve the legitimacy of numerous existing states. Palestinians have a legitimate national claim that can be addressed through negotiated borders, security arrangements, and self-determination; that claim does not require or justify denying the parallel Jewish claim or Israel’s existence as a recognized state. The practical outcome of the “no right to exist” position has been repeated rejection of partition offers (1947, 2000, 2008) in favor of maximalist demands. That is a political choice, not a historical necessity.

The Council of Clermont was a mixed synod of ecclesiastics and laymen of the Catholic Church, called by Pope Urban II and held from 17 to 27 November 1095 at Clermont, Auvergne, at the time part of the Duchy of Aquitaine.[1][2]

While the council is known today primarily for the speech Pope Urban gave on the final day, it was primarily a synod focused on implementing the Cluniac reforms, enacting decrees and settling local and regional issues.[3] This also included the extension of the excommunication of Philip I of France for his adulterous remarriage to Bertrade of Montfort and a declaration of renewal of the Truce of God, an attempt on the part of the church to reduce feuding among Frankish nobles.[4]

Pope Urban's speech on 27 November included the call to arms that would result in the First Crusade,[5] and eventually the capture of Jerusalem and the establishment of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. In this, Urban reacted to the request by Byzantine emperor Alexius I Comnenus who had sent envoys to the Council of Piacenza requesting military assistance against the Seljuk Turks.[6] Several accounts of the speech survive; of these, the one by Fulcher of Chartres, who was present at the council, is generally accepted as the most reliable.
