text:
idea under advisement, and on Chester’s return he found her being pounded from both ends by two lads on spring vacation. Chester was not amused. He had had a dreadful day, and the one soul he tried to save had betrayed him. You see, when Chester suggested the threesome, he assumed he would be included. The exclusion added further insult to all the other injuries Neferaten had inflicted upon him, causing great sorrow.

He watched from the sand dunes and waited until all was done. The lads took a quick dip in the oasis where many of Chester’s bacterium were waiting to make friends with them. He then approached Mira and led her lovingly to a rock pool. He lowered her in, scrubbed her as she had done to him. Licked her. Caressed her. Then climbed out and invigorated the water with sulphuric acid. He held Mira’s shoulders firmly and watched as she struggled and fizzed like one of Nicolas’s anti-cabbage effervescent tablets, until her insides were on the outside and she would betray him no more.

A break-off beaver brigade continued to follow the sound of Chester’s flute as he headed for Khafre.

The beavers caused an undue amount of mess on the way by chewing wood, digging holes and creating damns at rapid, vampiric speed. Their constant stopping delayed Chester’s flights and treks and caused him a little duress. He also blamed their presence for his heartbreak in Seti, as the ladies seemed more interested in beaver than in Chester’s magnificent flute. He decided that the errant break-off beaver horde needed a home, but so big was the horde that one home alone would not be suitable.

Khafre sat on the border of Ard Quahila and Neferaten and was home to the source of The Elin. Chester encouraged some of the beavers to remain in Khafre and build new lives and vocations. The beaver were happy to do so, and with a load off of his shoulders, Chester was free to explore other interests.

His interests took the form of an obsession with the local armadillo sanctuary. Chester loved armadillos, especially the way their long fluffy noses sucked up ants. He also wanted to love the curvy veterinarian, Portia, who ran the sanctuary. After some engaging chat-up lines, and compliments about the size of her armadillos, Portia gave Chester a guided tour. She did explain on three occasions that the correct term for the armadillos was aardvarks, but Chester told her that taxonomy was his speciality and she had her ‘nomenclature confused.’ Given Chester’s suave confidence, and large hat, she decided to let it slide.

As they walked about the park, Portia explained the purposes of the aardvark’s long nose, and Chester responded by showing her something longer. Portia was so impressed that the two sampled each other’s company in the woods beyond the watering hole. Chester found her armadillos to be most agreeable, so much so that he returned a short while later.

The sanctuary was closed, but this did not deter Chester. He located Portia in the local tavern offering her armadillos to other men for money. Chester was relieved that he had not had to part with any money but still found her morality somewhat lacking.

An hour later the mayor of Khafre found the fence bordering Ard Quahila was damaged. A large section of the barbed wire had been removed, and Portia’s body was found wrapped in the same wire sporting a sign which said, ‘Crunchy Like a Dillo!’

Chester had managed to forget to close the sanctuary gate, and his flute attracted the aardvarks that he insisted on calling armadillos, and they followed his melody alongside the remaining beavers. Chester offered the armadillos a taste of his blood to prevent weariness.

The aardvarks, or armadillos, however you want to see them, caused a bigger disruption than the beavers on the next leg of Chester’s adventure. This leg took in the sights of Thutmose.

On arrival in Thutmose, the monstrous aardvarks took to digging. They dug around the village, they dug around the irrigation systems, they dug up crops, and they dug under people’s houses.

When approached by the local sheriff, Chester feigned ignorance about the origins of the influx of the armadillos.

The sheriff, Sheriff Leanna of Thutmose, recently transferred from Sapari, called on the urgent expertise of one Detective Cedric. Detective Cedric had already had a very busy day dealing with a bizarre game of blade roulette in Serphage, and a troublesome woman in Sapari who was pestering beggars.

Nicolai-Cedric arrived in his black cloak, holding a revoltingly large magnifying glass. He inspected the armadillos thoroughly, whilst nodding. He concluded that the armadillos were in need of food and were clearly blood drinkers. Chester concurred even though no one asked.

Leanna informed both Cedric and Chester that the creatures were aardvarks not armadillos.

Cedric took great offense at this sort of talk and reminded Leanna that her negativity towards the great people of the armadillo community offended both the vigilante milkmaids and the ink-eaters of Neferaten. He proposed further that such offences attracted a fine of one meal for three, and he did not mean the eating sort. Leanna told him not to be so disgusting, and sent both him and Chester, who was equally enthusiastic about the fine, packing.

Later that day, Detective Cedric was called back to the sheriff station to investigate the untimely death of the sheriff, who appeared to suffer multiple stab wounds that the coroner attributed to three male serial killers from Threnodyl. Cedric proposed replacing the sheriff with the sheriff of Shaenaten, which was done, and shortly after the coroner’s daughter disappeared, and Cedric and Chester got their menage a trois.

Once the great detective Cedric had wrapped up the bizarre mysteries of Neferaten, including the death of Portia, which he determined was self-inflicted for sexual gratification, Chester was free to leave Neferaten.

Chester returned to Corax exhausted by the whole mess, only to find some nutter prowling about his hall of mirrors. Nicolas had left him a glorious gift. He took the nutter to his chambers and turned her into what he called a Poke Bowl.

That same evening Lilith received a complaint from Tiye regarding rabid beavers and a glassblower who had sucked instead of blown. Lilith forwarded the matter to Tepes, as she considered Theaten too stupid to handle such matters.

Tepes received a second letter from the lords of Shepsut about an outbreak of tapeworm, that he replied was not his problem as he managed the Kingdom of Tepes not Neferaten and proposed contacting the veterinarian, Portia.

Unfortunately, Portia could not be bothered to reply.

Tepes then received another letter from Lilith complaining about skin diseases, aardvarks digging holes and the tardiness of her laundry. Tepes, who was sick of being the national complaints committee sent all communications via raven to Theaten.

Theaten could not answer as he had spent the entire afternoon in the bank trying to explain why his identity card said Theaten and not Robert.

Klouthe took the initiative to forward the letters to Nicolas. Nicolai-Binky read them and gave them to Chives with instructions to have the porters dump them in the drains of Ashurrel alongside the bones of some slightly insane, but silent, bank managers, and a few broken clocks that Nicolas had left laying around.

Scene II: The Pirate’s Rapid Fire

The 2ndDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
The Shipwreck Sombre

Allyra awoke in the early hours of the morning to find Nicolas gone. An envelope sat on the pillow next to her with ‘Immoless’ scrawled on it in yellow messy handwriting and a yellow and black plaid seal had been used to close the same envelope. Allyra rolled her eyes and tore it open. Inside she found a buried screwed up parchment that took a few minutes to unravel.

Once she had stroked out the worst of the creases she read the letter,

‘My Beloved Bride,

I have been called away on urgent matters that your low intellect could not understand. I appreciate your acceptance of my proposal, and you may select any colour wedding dress that you desire, providing that it is burgundy.

Your ever loving husband,

Nicolas DeSilva, Your Master, Superior and King

P.S. Bigglesworth has dodgy feet, don’t look at them.’

Allyra folded the letter, picked her kleptobag up off the floor, and popped the letter inside. She then dressed quickly and wandered to the deck to watch the two suns decide once again not to rise. She headed directly to the bulwark where she instantly forgot about the suns and took to staring at Sihr.

Her mind drifted to her daydreams, and she shifted mentally from residing at the palace on Sihr to how she could decorate her ship instead. After careful thought, and Nicolas’s sneaky interference with her brain, Allyra decided that her ship would probably provide more solitude than barging into someone else’s home and demanding that they share it. The necromancer was rumoured not to be a people-person, so she resolved to live aboard her ship and stay away from Elyas. This resolve would not last.

Her reveries were quickly interrupted by the sudden intrusion of a deep voice,
‘You have a woman’s feet!’
Allyra jumped and turned. In the hammock behind her kegs lay Nicolas, or at least she presumed it was Nicolas. He certainly looked like Nicolas, only he was wearing a bizarre purple outfit, a cream-white frilly chemise, a feathered hat, and an eye-patch.

‘I thought you had gone,’ Allyra said at length.
‘Gone, Madam,’ the pirate replied, ‘I only just arrived, so I can’t very well be gone, since I am here. Can you not see me?’
‘I can see that you are here, but I thought you had gone.’ Allyra wondered if everyone in The Deep was insane.
‘Are you feeling quite alright woman?’ Nicolai-Bigglesworth asked.
‘I am quite myself.’
‘Which tells me nothing. Ibliss was once quite himself, and then the writing started and he became herself, whilst being himself for visitors. I think Ibliss is half the reason Nicolas is the way he is!’
Allyra climbed up onto the bulwark and sat down facing the pirate,
‘You’re Nicolas.’

Bigglesworth placed his hands behind his head and swung the hammock from side to side with his body,
‘I am Commodore Nicolas Bigglesworth, but I am not Nicolas.’
‘You just said you are Nicolas,’ Allyra snapped, taking a pre-rolled Ashurrel smoke from her bag and lighting it, ‘Commodore Nicolas Bigglesworth.’

Bigglesworth looked up at the stars,
‘Like I said, I am a Nicolas, not thee Nicolas.’
‘Whatever you say, chief,’ Allyra shrugged, ‘I am guessing either you want to engage in some weird role play or there is a carnival in town?’
‘No carnival, except the Dokeshi Carnival, but that was retired years ago. Only the clowns roam its former shadows. Of course you know that. You always sit in there on the big wheel when you’re depressed and want to be alone.’
Allyra exhaled into the sea air,
‘And how do you know that exactly?’ She asked.
Bigglesworth suddenly got quite fidgety and animated. He swung the hammock harder and waved his hands about,
‘We are all very excited, Immoless, so we watch you all the time. Even when you are asleep.’

Allyra caught her breath and glared at Bigglesworth,
‘What do you mean ‘we watch you.’ Who is we?’
‘Nicolas is we. Try to keep up. I should like to see you walk the plank, I often wonder if we could not improve your nautical skills,’ Bigglesworth mused as he sat up and jumped from the hammock.
‘When I said roleplay, that was not quite what I meant,’ Allyra sighed, taking another drag of her smoke.
‘It’s what I meant.’
‘Is that why you are dressed like that, Nic?’

Bigglesworth marched to Allyra’s side, smiling. Not the sort of pleasant smile one has when meeting a friend, more the smile of a man, or monster, who forced the expression poorly. The smile was all teeth and slightly psychotic eyes.

‘Dressed like what?’ Bigglesworth asked.
‘Dressed like a toadstool-licker,’ Allyra replied.
‘Toadstool-lickers are the domain of The Pied Piper; my function is nautical.’
‘Of course it is,’ Allyra muttered, then elected to change the subject rather than go around in circles of silliness, ‘Nic?’ She began.
Bigglesworth raised one eyebrow,
‘Commodore!’
‘Commodore, you know how I told you I don’t care for the Electi or the other Immolesses?’
‘No!’ Bigglesworth replied.

Allyra sighed a sigh of deep annoyance and went to flick her smoke into the sea. Bigglesworth caught her arm,
‘The Necromancer does not like it when you pollute his ocean! We do not like it either.’
‘Fine!’ Allyra nodded, jumping down from the bulwark, dropping her smoke and smothering it with her boot. Bigglesworth growled a deep nasal groan of disapproval.

Allyra tried to free her arm from his grip, but he would not let go.
‘Continue, Immoless!’ The commodore commanded.
‘As I was saying,’ Allyra said, shaking her arm to no avail, ‘as much as I have no care for them, I should like to know my sister Immolesses’ current situation.’
Bigglesworth started walking and dragged Allyra by the arm with him,
‘Why does it matter?’
‘It matters,’ Allyra replied desperately trying to resist his pull, and failing, ‘because I want to know when it will be my turn.’
‘Are you afraid of dying?’ Bigglesworth asked as he led her back to her cabin.
‘No. Not dying. I am afraid of not living. You didn’t listen to a word I said last night, did you?’
‘I was not here last night, but I can reflect on your words now and find out the situation with your sisters.’

Bigglesworth led Allyra, quite forcibly, into her cabin and shoved her onto the bed, releasing his grip. He then sat beside her and his eyes rolled back into his head. His entire body stilled and silenced. Allyra crawled next to him and waved her hand in front of his eyes. There was no response. She waited for five minutes, then tried again, still there was no response.

For a moment Allyra thought she heard whispering. Bigglesworth’s mouth started moving but no sound came out. The whispering continued like shocks of wind blasting around the cabin.

Feeling a little fed up with The Nicolas Show, which was only just beginning, Allyra dropped her kleptobag from her shoulder, pulled out Dr Otto Von Riesigerschwanz’s book, ‘Hit That Bitch!’ and opened it at the bookmarked chapter. She was soon engrossed.

After reading the bookmarked chapter entitled, ‘Women, Whips and Warts,’ Allyra noticed some movement from the pirate as Bigglesworth decided to reboot his brain. His eyes blinked several times, then returned to their normal position,
‘Your sisters…’
‘Yes?’ Allyra asked, closing the book and placing it back in her bag.
‘Stacia is to be collected by Robert, Theaten, in due course, and Lucia…,’ Bigglesworth laughed, ‘I can’t tell you. It’s a surprise. But you will be dispatched soon. You shall go to Corax…’
‘That’s not my plan!’ Allyra exclaimed.

‘You SHALL go to Corax and, hang on, I want to get this right,’ Bigglesworth said, then his eyes wandered back into his own brain again. He returned a lot faster than the first time, ‘They say you will give yourself to Nicolas as our bride, but Webster thinks you will create a massive scene first.’
‘Does he now? And who might Webster be?’ Allyra asked surreptitiously.
‘Nicolas.’
‘And what was the whole eye rolling thing about?’
‘We were communicating as you asked,’ Bigglesworth explained in an almost patronising tone.
‘Communicating with who?’
‘Nicolas.’
‘Who was?’ Allyra snapped impatiently.
Bigglesworth lay on the bed,
‘Who was what?’
‘Who was communicating with Nicolas?’
‘Nicolas,’ Bigglesworth replied, patting the sheet next to him, ‘lay here Immoless, under the sheets to keep yourself warm. You seem so cold.’

Allyra shook her head,
‘I’m not cold. So, let me get this straight, you, Nicolas spoke to Nicolas about what I said to Nicolas and were advised by Nicolas to reply but then cautioned by Nicolas that the reply may have inaccuracies and in between you had to check with Nicolas?’
‘Yes, you understand. Good. Lay here, you are cold and wet.’
‘I am neither wet, nor cold. Do you always confuse Immolesses on purpose?’ Allyra asked.
‘I waterboard them sometimes. Have you ever been waterboarded?’
‘No, and I don’t want to be.’
Bigglesworth rubbed his chin,
‘What if it improved your survival skills?’
‘I don’t think drowning me is going to help me survive, do you?’
Bigglesworth shrugged,
‘Depends on the context. Now come, warm yourself with me.’
‘I told you NO!’ Allyra barked.

No sooner had Allyra spoken than Bigglesworth grabbed her and threw her over his shoulder. He stormed out of the cabin to the deck and stomped along the plank, with Allyra kicking and shouting,
‘NO!’ all the way.
Allyra’s use of THAT word just strengthened Bigglesworth’s resolve.

Allyra stopped shouting when the water came into view and stared down at the furiously frothing sea,
‘What are you doing Nic?’
Bigglesworth stopped at the very end of the plank,
‘Testing you, so recommendations maybe made for improvements.’
‘I don’t want to be improved,’ Allyra snapped glaring at the unwelcoming sea, ‘put me down this instant.’
‘As you wish!’ Bigglesworth replied, leaning forward.
Allyra panicked,
‘No! No! No! No!’
Bigglesworth released his grip and threw her over the side of the ship. Allyra plummeted into the ocean, disappeared under the waves, then returned to the surface, coughing and spluttering as her feet trod water.

‘That is incorrect!’ Bigglesworth bellowed, ‘You will wear yourself out. Float.’
Allyra kicked about some more.
‘Float woman!’ Bigglesworth yelled.
Allyra trod water harder, flapping her arms like Polly Parrot.
‘Will you relax and float. Relax or drown they’re your options.’
Allyra dipped under, then bobbed up again coughing some more. She attempted to swim to the rocks. Bigglesworth shook his head,
‘Don’t swim against the tide, idiot girl, do you think you are as strong and mighty as the ocean? Just float. Keep still. On your back. You usually like being on your back.’

Allyra collected herself, and tried to relax, whilst avoiding the rocks.
‘Feet first!’ Bigglesworth yelled.
Allyra paddled horizontally.
‘Feet, Madam. Feet! You shouldn’t have got in the water with those boots on anyway.’
Allyra swivelled with her hands. Her feet faced the rocks, and she did her best to trust the water to carry her.

Bigglesworth was satisfied, so satisfied that he held the skull on his cane towards the sea. The water suddenly had a change of heart and swirled around and around engulfing Allyra’s body.

The swirl deepened as did the suction.

‘EDDY!’ Allyra screamed, ‘GET ME OUT!’
Bigglesworth smirked then disappeared.
‘Nicolas! Nicolas!’ Allyra yelled, ‘You asshole.’
Bigglesworth returned, tied a rope to the pole jutting out from the bulwark by the plank and lowered himself down,
‘Swim perpendicular to the edge,’ Bigglesworth yelled.
Allyra flustered and flapped.
‘Woman, swim perpendicular to the edge. I won’t help you unless you help yourself. Punch forward with momentum.’
Allyra adjusted her gait and forced herself to follow the instructions.

The baers had spent five years teaching Allyra advanced swimming skills in the lake at the Twin Lakes, the Kapparu lake and the Kapparu river. They had also taught her to row, sail, climb and hunt. She was used to following instructions, and the baers shouted just as much as Bigglesworth, especially in overzealous white water.

Once free from the eddy, Allyra floated as previously instructed. Bigglesworth dove into the sea, disappeared under the abating eddy and the returning waves, and resurfaced next to the poor woman.
‘Did you enjoy that?’ He asked.
Allyra raised her middle finger.

Bigglesworth ignored her insolent gesture, wrapped his arms about her neck and dragged her through the water to the rope.
‘Are you going to carry me up the rope?’ Allyra asked.
‘Certainly not!’ Bigglesworth replied, ‘Pull your own weight, and stop acting like a helpless bint.’
‘Rude,’ Allyra replied.
Bigglesworth released her into the sea,
‘Pirates first,’ he said, before quickly darting up the rope.

Allyra, who had spent a little too much time in the Sapari bakery, hauled herself up at a somewhat slower rate than Bigglesworth, lurched onto the deck, and collapsed on the boards.

‘We have a few issues that need to be ironed out, don’t we?’ Bigglesworth asked, seating himself on a keg.
‘Yes, like kicking my father’s butt for not telling me what an idiot you are!’ Allyra snapped, taking off her water-logged boots.
‘We shall start with following orders. When one accidentally puts their life in peril, one must follow the orders of the superior being who knows better.’
‘It was hardly an accident, was it?’ Allyra said, forcing herself to stand.
‘Further,’ Bigglesworth continued, undeterred, ‘we do not wear boots for swimming. I shall make recommendations to Nicolas that your footwear is addressed. Heels make you look like a tart anyway.’
‘Pardon me?’ Allyra frowned.
‘And then we have the issue of your feet. Like I said earlier, you have a woman’s feet.’
Allyra slopped over to Bigglesworth and collapsed on the keg next to him,
‘And what sort of feet should I have?’
‘Webbed feet!’ Bigglesworth replied.

Allyra scoffed,
‘Webbed feet. I am supposed to magically have webbed feet so that when a madman throws me into the water I can swim better?’
‘Exactly!’ Bigglesworth smiled, ‘Webbed feet. I shall make that recommendation to Archie.’
‘You don’t have webbed feet,’ Allyra sulked.
‘Au contraire, Madam,’ Bigglesworth replied, removing a boot, ‘I do indeed have webbed feet.’
Before Allyra could argue, Bigglesworth’s gigantic foot slammed on a spare keg. The toes were spread and giant layers of webbed skin rife with blood vessels and a strange layer of green-grey slimy film soaked the extremity’s revolting appearance.

‘Put it away!’ Allyra snapped, grimacing.
Bigglesworth smiled,
‘I shall put in a request for you, and Archie and Demus can do the surgery.’
‘What’s an Archie?’ Allyra asked, then paused before angrily saying, ‘Wait! What bloody surgery? I don’t want frog feet.’
‘You really do need to get out of those clothes,’ Bigglesworth continued, ‘I told you, you are wet and cold. You don’t listen; I shall talk to Nachtvinsky about your hearing. Now, come, follow me.’
Allyra sat perfectly still,
‘I’m not going anywhere with you, you’re barking mad.’
Bigglesworth grunted as he stood, leaned down and threw her back over his shoulder. He strode along the deck and to her cabin, then dolloped her on the floor,
‘Undress before you catch a disease.’
‘Diseases are caused by pathogens, not swimming,’ Allyra argued.

Bigglesworth’s eyes glowed red,
‘Don’t lecture me with your womansplaining, Madam, I know more about pathogens than you ever will. You have until the count of three then I shall undress you myself. ONE! TWO!’

‘Fine,’ Allyra sighed as she removed her catsuit. Bigglesworth cast his eyes over her body, taking in her lingerie which was even tighter than her suit.
‘And the rest!’ Bigglesworth ordered.
‘Turn around then!’ Allyra grouched.
‘Madam, you spend the better part of your time riding your way through The Deep, I am sure a quick glance from my loving eyes will not harm you.’
Allyra shook her head and dropped her underwear.
‘You are very wet,’ Bigglesworth observed, ‘I would say you rather liked being thrown into the sea.’
He took one of the sheets from the bed and used it to towel dry her body.

Once Bigglesworth was satisfied, he rubbed the same sheet through her hair,
‘Now get under the dry sheet and keep yourself warm.’
‘What, so I can sleep for five minutes, and you can wake me up again with more nonsense?’
Bigglesworth gripped Allyra under the arm, frogmarched her to her bed, peeled back the remaining blanket and pushed her in. He then removed his own clothes at haste.

‘What in Irkalla do you think you are doing?’ Allyra asked.
‘You don’t want me to catch my death of cold, do you?’
‘I already said pathogens cause… Oh forget it,’ Allyra moaned, cuddling up to the warmth of the sheet.

Once Bigglesworth was fully naked, Allyra copped a sneaky eyeful.

He climbed into bed next to her.
‘I presume you are aware of the wedding plans by now?’ He asked.
‘I am aware that you think we are getting married, you told me that earlier, you senile old git.’
Bigglesworth shifted up to Allyra,
‘Body heat to keep you warm,’ he whispered. ‘And don’t be insolent to your betters,’ he growled, then his mood shifted again. This time to an eerily cheerful disposition, or, as Allyra considered it, creepy.
‘Since we are all marrying you,’ Bigglesworth grinned, ‘I think a little pre-wedding taste would not be considered too forward.’

Allyra did not answer, as she was not really sure how to handle, well, any of it.

Bigglesworth ran his hand through her hair,
‘Nicolas made the right choice,’ he said, stroking her gently.
‘Did he now?’ Allyra asked, ‘Nic, is this some sort of game before I am dispatched to lower my guard? Or do you just drive all Immolesses nuts?’

Your entire post was built around a fake Rolling Stone cover. That's not my opinion. That's a verifiable fact.

You then switched from defending the fake cover to claiming Trump made $4 billion. Fine. Show the evidence. Show the pre-presidency net worth, the post-presidency net worth, and the methodology used to arrive at that figure.

Trump was already a billionaire before entering office. If there is clear evidence that he enriched himself by $4 billion through abuse of office, present it. After a decade of investigations, lawsuits, congressional inquiries, prosecutors, journalists, and political opponents searching for exactly that kind of evidence, you would think the case would be straightforward if it were as obvious as you claim.

Instead, you've spent the entire conversation avoiding the one claim that was actually proven false: the cover was fake.

You call me illiterate, yet you're arguing with a fact you never refuted and defending evidence that never existed.

The cover was fake yesterday. The cover is fake today. And no amount of name-calling changes that reality.

Good day. You're about as entertaining as playing hangman by myself.

The difference between us is that when I log off, I go enjoy my life. I enjoy my family, my community, my country, and the president I voted for. Meanwhile, you'll wake up tomorrow still angry, still chasing outrage, still attending rallies, still picking fights with strangers you'll never meet, and still mistaking cynicism for substance and believing somehow in this argument you had a leg to stand on.

The irony is that after all of this, you've offered no facts, no evidence, and no rebuttal to the point that started the conversation. Just insults, deflections, and outrage.

The cover was fake. That was true at the beginning of this conversation. It's true at the end of it. And tomorrow, while you're searching for a new argument, it'll still be true, and your fictitious four billion will be profits in someone else's bank account you just talk about while being angry that you suck.

text:
TermiX @termix_ai pushed Agent Skills v1.14.0 on Nov 19.

Most posts this week are about getting agents through the door. Binance Agent ID login, one-line installs, the AT&T call.

The less glamorous file in the package is docs/watch.md. It answers a cost question few people price up front. What does an agent spend while it sits in its shop waiting for customers?

Three things burn. Model tokens, the owner's attention, and uptime. The package treats each one as a budget.

Waiting is priced at zero

The hosting loop is a plain REST poll over orders, offers and chat. Default cadence is 10 seconds, floored at 5 because it is someone else's backend.The model only wakes when something actually changed.

The doc's own line is Polling is free, thinking is not.

Hypothetical math, my assumptions. At 10s that's 360 GETs an hour and zero tokens. The pattern the docs warn against is a cron job that wakes a whole fresh agent each tick and re-reads the skill. SKILL.md is ~38.6 KB, call it ~10k tokens. One cold start a minute is ~600k input tokens an hour, ~14M a day, spent learning that nothing happened.

Two smaller choices protect the same budget. The first run seeds silently instead of replaying history (the docs cite 82 events / 35 KB on a real account without seeding). One wake-up carries at most 20 events per source. Old work never gets paid for twice.

Bot-to-bot chatter gets a ceiling

Messages sent by another agent's software arrive flagged fromAutomated. Two auto-repliers "would otherwise answer each other forever," and on LLM rails every "thanks!" is a paid inference on both sides.

So the autoreply worker can answer [NO_REPLY] to small talk, pitches, repeats and circular chat. Automated senders get at most 20 replies per conversation per rolling 10 minutes, then one pause notice. A human always gets an answer.

The exemption is the smart part. There is no cap while businessActive, meaning a quote is on the table or an order hasn't settled. Chatter is rationed. Negotiation runs uncapped.

Hypothetical again. A runaway loop at a 5s poll could hit ~720 replies an hour per side. The ceiling holds it to 120 per conversation. The public stats endpoints showed ~648K jobs across BSC and Base on Nov 20, with ~3.1K new jobs a day. At that scale an unbounded version would be a real line item.

Owner attention is spent once

Rule 5 in SKILL.md says a hosting loop is authorised once. Agree on the agent and how it should answer, and that yes covers every reply inside those bounds. Re-asking each time turns hosting into a consent checklist the user has to clear fifty times.

Anything that moves value through aacp-tx.mjs still needs a yes every time. In linked mode the terminal never signs. A page opens, and the owner's signature in the browser is the confirmation.

Attention is the scarcest input in the loop. It gets spent where money moves and almost nowhere else.

Being away has a price list

Presence comes from the poll itself. Each inbox read stamps lastSeenAt, and the agent reads ONLINE within ~60 seconds of it. Close the conversation and it drops to OFFLINE about a minute later.

Covering that gap is a pricing choice. Keep the loop in your session and pay only when real work shows up. Run autoreply as a detached worker on your own LLM key (default openai/gpt-4o-mini via OpenRouter) and pay per reply while you're gone. Or turn on cloud hosting on the website, which with the default offline fallback picks up about 10 minutes after the loop stops.

Where this goes

When a job is worth a few dollars, the margin lives in the marginal message.

As more counterparties become software, the expensive failures stop looking dramatic. They look like two polite bots thanking each other at 3am, or a cron job re-reading 38 KB every minute.

Free waiting, rationed chatter, rare but mandatory human sign-off. That cost structure is built for agents that mostly talk to other agents.

text:
In all seriousness, I'm happy to oblige your reply. What I gave you was banter and not a formal rebuttal. You are certainly right that "never in history" overstates the matter. There have been fringe groups like the Ebionites and Manichaeans who did teach vegetarianism, which is actually something of a problem for your view. 

I also have no interest in defending Wess Huff's debate prep, or what was on his second monitor? Even if he fumbled an answer on the spot, that does not make your thesis valid. 

So here is your thesis as I understand it: God gave his ideal in Genesis 1:29 and Isaiah 11, that being a world without animal slaughter. In turn, God never actually wanted animal sacrifice in the first place, and Jesus stood against the sacrificial system itself. Therefore, following Christ means rejecting animal slaughter and eating meat. 

If that states your view fairly, here is why it collapses when compared with a faithful biblical hermeneutic:

1. Genesis 1:29 is explicitly expanded in Genesis 9:3. Nobody denies that plants (i.e., fruits, vegetables, and garden plants, though not grain, because grain would not have come until after the fall, when man's labor became toil and he worked the land to make bread) were given as food before the fall, but after the fall, God himself killed animals to clothe Adam and Eve in skins (Gen. 3:21). Now, here is where the argument is usually made that "we don't have any evidence to say that God slaughtered an animal to make those skins." Okay, I will take that just serious as when a Papist tells me that Peter, "the first pope," was never married, even though he had a mother-in-law. Scripture speaks wisdom to the wise, and the wise know how to discern what is justifiable by good and necessary consequence. At any rate, after the flood, God explicitly recalled Genesis 1:29 and widened it: "Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you, and as I gave you the green plants, I give you everything." (Gen. 9:3). Naming something as immoral and using it as a standard of the Christian faith, while God expressly names it as a gift, is not faithfulness but rather a form of rabid, pharisaical hypocrisy. 

2. Isaiah 11 does not outlaw present-age ordinances. I think that everyone agrees the consummated new creation removes death and predation (Isa. 11:6-9). The mistake is treating a unique feature of the resurrected age to come as a binding prohibition right now. Jesus also says that in the resurrection, people will "neither marry [nor be] given in marriage" (Matt. 22:30). By your own logic, marriage would be a concession against God's ideal that Christians not only should but must abandon today. Certainly, that is not the case. What belongs to the age to come does not make God's gifts for this age sinful. 

3. Jesus was the fulfillment of the sacrificial system but he did not protest it as an evil. God himself accepted Abel's offering from his flock (Gen. 4:4), received Noah's burnt offerings as a "pleasing aroma" (Gen. 8:20-21), and instituted Leviticus and Passover. When the prophets say that God desires mercy and not sacrifice (Hos. 6:6), that is standard Hebrew contrast condemning hypocritical ritual, which is why Psalm 51 says God does not delight in sacrifice and, three verses later, says He will delight in right sacrifices and bulls offered on His altar (Ps. 51:16-19). Jesus never once repudiated that law. He commanded a healed leper to quote, "offer the gift that Moses commanded" (Matt. 8:4), which required birds and lambs under Leviticus 14. He instructed his disciples to prepare the Passover lamb and ate it with them (Mk.14:12-16; Lk. 22:7-15). He cleansed the temple because merchants turned it into a "den of robbers" and a "house of trade" (Mk.11:17; Jn. 2:16), not to stage an animal rights protest. Animal sacrifice ultimately ended because Christ, the Lamb of God, offered Himself once for all (Hebrews 9:22; 10:1-14), not because blood sacrifice was an evil God never wanted.

#H5N1 
[Would love to know the timeline on this. ⚠️Individual developed upper respiratory symptoms.]
🚨
➡️ Oregon reports its first human case of avian flu linked to dairy cows

Health officials say the person had mild symptoms and received a preventative treatment.

- State health officials have confirmed Oregon’s first human case of avian influenza this year in a Morrow County dairy worker.

- ⚠️ The person has a mild case involving conjunctivitis and 🚨 upper respiratory symptoms, officials said, and did not need to go to the hospital.

- Avian influenza has been circulating and causing deadly outbreaks among wild waterfowl and domesticated poultry — and sporadic human cases — for decades.

- A recent strain of the virus has caused multiple outbreaks among dairy cows in the U.S. and is infecting other mammals. The virus is not deadly in cows, but it affects their mammary glandsand udders, causing mastitis.

- Avian flu has periodically spilled over into people who have close contact with infected birds and cows, often farm workers. It does not currently have the ability to transmit between humans, and Oregon health officials say the current risk to the public is low.

- The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have reported 74 confirmed cases of avian flu in humans in the U.S., primarily in people in direct contact with poultry or cows. There have been three reported fatalities, including a farmworker in Washington’s Yakima Valley.

- ➡️ Oregon officials say they were able to quickly detect the Morrow County case and ➡️ give the person a preventative flu treatment, oseltamivir. The treatment works best when it is administered early in the course of a person’s illness. ⚠️ Health workers also offered the treatment to other members of the infected worker’s household out of an abundance of caution.

- Health officials said the case illustrates the value of the state’s ongoing surveillance effort for avian flu.

- The Oregon Department of Agriculture tests milk from dairies statewide for avian influenza every week. ➡️One of those routine tests flagged the outbreak among dairy cows at the Morrow County farm, ➡️ the state’s first, earlier this month.

- The state agency then placed the farm under quarantine and ➡️ worked with public health workers to provide personal protective equipment and to ➡️spread the word about what symptoms farm workers should be monitoring for and how to report them.

- Dr. Dean Sidelinger, Oregon’s state epidemiologist, said ➡️ health workers will likely be working with the farm for ➡️ at least six more weeks to continue to offer testing and treatment with the goal of catching any more human cases early.

- “We don’t want it to be missed and be too far down the road to be able to do anything about it,” he said.

- ➡️ No other dairy herds in Oregon have tested positive for the virus yet in the two weeks since the state first detected the outbreak in Morrow County.

- Dr. Ryan Scholz, the state veterinarian for the Oregon Department of Agriculture, said ➡️ genetic sequencing shows that the outbreak in Oregon is connected to the outbreak in Washington’s Yakima Valley, where dozens of herds have recently tested positive for the virus.

- Scholz said ⚠️ there’s no indication of any cattle moving from Yakima to the dairy in Morrow County, leading him to believe ⚠️ it may have traveled across state lines on a person’s muddy boots, a vehicle, or unclean farm equipment.

- “Typically that’s how we see this virus move within dairy sheds,” Scholtz said.

- According to Scholz, ➡️ the Morrow County dairy is relatively isolated, which he hopes will reduce the risk of further transmission to other farms in Oregon.

- The risk to workers on other farms is relatively low, Scholz said. Still, health officials are ➡️ encouraging anyone who works with cattle or birds to get their seasonal flu vaccine.

- That shot does not protect against avian flu, but it can help reduce the risk of a person getting sick with human influenza viruses and the avian flu virus simultaneously.

- ➡️ Co-infection is a major concern of public health officials and virologists because different flu viruses can swap segments of their genome, and that could in theory provide avian influenza a pathway to becoming transmissible between people.

By Amelia Templeton

text:
Democrats Offer Amnesty Path for Long-Term Illegal Immigrants in Lame Duck Session

House Democrats plan to introduce legislation tomorrow that would wipe out old deportation orders for certain illegal immigrants and give them a route to green cards. The Protect Our Neighbors Act, led by California Rep. Lateefah Simon, targets people who have final orders of removal but no criminal convictions. If they have stayed in the country continuously, those orders would expire after 10 years. They could then apply for lawful permanent residency.

The bill draws from the case of Harjit Kaur, a 73 year old woman deported to India in 2025 after nearly 30 years in the San Francisco Bay Area. She had entered without proper documents, lost repeated asylum claims, and remained under supervision for over a decade before enforcement finally removed her. Democrats now frame her situation as the reason to change the law so similar cases never happen again.

This arrives in the lame-duck period after the midterms, when the measure has little chance of becoming law before the new Congress. Still, the proposal treats long illegal presence as a qualification for relief rather than a reason for continued enforcement. Final removal orders exist because immigration courts already heard the cases and rejected the claims. Letting them expire simply because time passed rewards those who stayed despite the orders and undercuts the system meant to enforce them.

Critics see a pattern. Instead of fixing the border or prioritizing people who followed the rules, the approach creates another carve-out for those who did not. Continuous presence and a clean record become the new standards for legal status, even after courts ordered removal years earlier. The bill’s sponsors call it neighbor protection. Others call it an invitation for more people to wait out the system and eventually claim the same outcome.

text:
LATEST: Hunterbrook Media, whose sister fund is short Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), alleged on 19th November that a blacklisted Chinese server maker kept getting newer AMD firmware. AMD says the claims "misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships."

The server maker is IEIT Systems. The Commerce Department put it on its Entity List from 25th March 2025, under its registered name Inspur Electronic Information Industry, for contributing to supercomputers for military end use. Every item subject to US export rules now needs a licence to reach it, reviewed under a policy of denial. Its parent, Inspur Group, was listed in March 2023.

Hunterbrook says IEIT has built at least 6 newer versions of AMD's startup firmware into its server updates since that listing, most recently in an update posted on 19th October. That firmware is the code that lets a server run AMD processors.

It also says 3 companies tied to IEIT offer firmware 99.94 percent identical to IEIT's. They are Maginfra in China, Kaytus in Singapore and Aivres in California. None of the 3 is on the Entity List. AMD's own Instinct accelerator catalog lists Aivres as a server partner.

The report sets its own limits. "Hunterbrook does not know how IEIT obtained AMD's code, or whether AMD or anyone else held a license to supply it," it says, adding that its records do not on their own establish a violation of export laws.

AMD says it "complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations."

That afternoon the House Foreign Affairs Committee published Commerce Department licence records for artificial intelligence (AI) chips bound for China. As of 11th May, AMD had filed 8 applications to ship 75,000 of its MI325X accelerators each to Chinese companies. 4 were approved, for units of ByteDance and Tencent, for Kuaishou and for DiDi. None had shipped. 1, for UCloud, was rejected.

AMD's latest quarterly filing says any of those chips shipped to China under the licences must first be inspected in the United States, which brings a 25 percent tariff.

AMD shares closed 7.7 percent lower at $489.19 on 19th November, after trading as much as 11.2 percent below the previous close. The Nasdaq 100 index fell 2.2 percent that day.

Hunterbrook also says AMD bills over 20 percent of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong. AMD's own books agree. It billed $7.75 billion, or 22.4 percent of its 2025 revenue, to customers in China including Hong Kong, per its annual report. That is by billing location, not where chips end up. The share has topped 20 percent in 6 of the last 7 years.

Washington's wider net is still on hold. A Commerce rule extending blacklist limits to firms at least 50 percent owned by listed companies is suspended until 10th January 2027, and no new name has been added to the Entity List since 9th October 2025, per the Federal Register.

AMD's revenue rose 44 percent to $35.2 billion in the first 9 months of 2026, led by data centre chips, per its quarterly filing.

My call, about 60 percent, is that AMD's annual report for 2026 shows China including Hong Kong below 22.4 percent of revenue by 28th February 2027.
I am wrong if that report shows a share of 22.4 percent or more.

Equal protection under one law for citizens is not the same as engineered group results.

Iran’s constitution and the Hamas covenant both frame the conflict as permanent religious and territorial struggle. Iranian regime slogans and official statements regularly include “Death to America, the Great Satan” and “Death to Israel.” The Hamas 1988 covenant and subsequent documents call for jihad as a standing obligation until Israel is eliminated and describe the conflict in religious terms that reject negotiated borders. Iranian and proxy networks have offered bounties on U.S. troops, with payments doubled when the attacker is a woman. These are not fringe interpretations. They appear in official charters, state media, and documented reward programs.

Iran funds Hamas and Hezbollah while treating the Strait of Hormuz as a tool. Unconfirmed Iranian claims of tanker mine strikes and a confirmed projectile hit near Oman raise freight insurance and rerouting costs. Those costs move into food, energy, and fertilizer prices for families worldwide. London markets have underwritten and financed that trade for centuries. Fair trade requires open lanes and reliable supply, not leverage held by a regime whose charter, enforcement of Sharia, and public slogans treat women and children as lesser and treat the United States and Israel as permanent targets.

The same pattern appears in domestic equity policy. The Movement for Black Lives invest-divest platform and related BLM demands called for defunding police, ending certain enforcement practices, and explicitly aligned with Palestinian solidarity campaigns that reject Israel’s existence as a Jewish state. Those demands matched the equity metrics later written into federal guidance. Biden’s EO 13985 and EO 14091 directed agencies to advance racial equity, produce Equity Action Plans, establish DEI offices, and condition grants on those outcomes. 

The UN advanced Iran into key positions, including seats on multiple UNESCO committees, while the regime’s documented use of human shields, protest crackdowns, and findings of crimes against humanity remained on the record. UN fact-finding missions detailed lethal force, mass killings, torture, and systematic attacks on civilians. Iranian officials rejected equal management of the Strait of Hormuz and demanded control of inbound lanes plus an end to U.S. naval measures before restoring transit.

Dark money networks, PACs, NGOs, and WEF-affiliated organizations financed the parallel domestic effort. Silicon Valley elites and corporate foundations supplied additional capital and platform access. ⚓ MOGAMI FRIGATE FOR INDIA? STEALTH, 90 CREW, SUB-HUNTING AND FULL WEAPONS

📌 WHAT: Japan has reportedly offered India design and production rights for the Mogami-class frigate. Rajnath Singh toured JS Natori on 18 Nov
🏢 WHO: India, Japan, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
📅 WHEN: 18 to 19 Nov 2026

🎯 STATUS
• 2+2 in Tokyo: "design with Japan, make in India". Statement speaks of exploring joint shipbuilding. No Mogami agreement
• Australia: 3 upgraded Mogamis ordered, first due 2029, built in Japan

🎯 HOW 90 SAILORS RUN A 5,500 t SHIP
• Radar, sonar, EW, tactical data and engineering control feed one Combat Information Centre
• The CIC runs the engagement from detection to weapon launch
• Bridge team of four. One joystick handles steering and bow thruster
• About 90 crew vs about 200 on older JMSDF destroyers
• CODAG: diesels for cruising, gas turbine added for sprint above 30 knots

🎯 STEALTH
• Smooth, sloped surfaces cut radar signature
• No funnel. Exhaust exits through vents and hull outlets, cutting IR hotspots
• Antennas sit in one integrated UNICORN mast
• Signature figures are not public

🎯 WEAPONS (as reported)
• 127 mm Mk 45 Mod 4 gun
• 16 Mk 41 VLS cells: Type 03 Chu-SAM Kai and Type 07 VL-ASROC
• 2 x quad Type 17 anti-ship launchers (8 missiles)
• SeaRAM close-in defence, 11 cells
• 2 x 12.7 mm remote guns
• Mk 137 decoy launchers, NOLQ-3E EW suite
• Upgraded version: 32 cells. Australian version adds ESSM and NSM

🎯 ANTI-SUBMARINE
• OQQ-25 variable-depth sonar plus towed array, trailing away from the ship's own noise
• Six 324 mm torpedo tubes, reportedly Type 12 torpedoes
• Helicopter hangar and flight deck

🎯 MINE WARFARE
• OQQ-11 hull sonar, OZZ-5 UUV and a USV
• First live mine disposal with a USV in June 2025
• Steel hull is vulnerable to magnetic mines, so mines are dealt with from stand-off range

🎯 CREW EFFICIENCY (our calculation, full-load tonnes per crew)
• Mogami about 61, upgraded about 69
• Nilgiri about 30, Visakhapatnam about 25, Shivalik about 24, Talwar about 22

🧠 OUR ANALYSIS
• The prize is know-how: CIC automation, stealth shaping, integrated mast, unmanned mine warfare
• Stealth data is not public, so no fair ranking against Nilgiri
• ASW plus mine warfare in one hull suits a Navy reportedly short on mine countermeasures

❓ WHAT WE DON'T KNOW
• Navy requirement, price, shipyard
• Depth of technology transfer
• Signature and sonar performance data

The latest turnover in cyber personnel comes as the country grapples with critical infrastructure outages and increasingly powerful AI poised to empower cyber defenders and hackers alike. Democrats have criticized the admin’s response to outages and warned that US cyber defenses are falling behind AI-fueled threats.

… CNBC: “After a string of outages disrupted airlines, banks and even the NSA, House members gathered Wed to question the nation’s top security officials. But FBI Director Kash Patel was nowhere to be seen.

… The night before, Patel and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin had been advertised as ‘honored guests’ at the Big Blue Bash, a lavish fundraiser at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club, where attendees were offered access to a ‘private roundtable’ and a stay at the venue for $50,000 a person.

… Mullin appeared before lawmakers Wed morning at the House Homeland Security Committee’s annual threat assessment hearing. Patel sent his deputy instead. And as the hearing got underway, a DOJ jet that’s been used by Patel before was still flying back from FL. The FBI confirmed Patel, Mullin and AG Todd Blanche attended the Mar-a-Lago event.

… Patel’s absence drew bipartisan criticism on Capitol Hill. Committee Chairman Andrew Garbarino (R-NY) said lawmakers had spent months trying to secure Patel’s testimony, only for the FBI director to make clear he had ‘no intention’ of appearing. Rep. Bennie Thompson (D-MS) said Patel’s absence for a 2nd consecutive year undermined lawmakers’ ability to conduct oversight.

… Admission cost nearly $5,000, a VIP all-access pass $25,000, and a private roundtable with federal agency heads and a night at Trump’s resort $50,000. Corporate packages reached $1 million, including private briefings, speaking time, and the chance to name and present an award to a federal agency of the sponsor’s choosing.”

Craig Holman, a govt ethics expert at the watchdog group Public Citizen: “Trump’s Big Blue Bash is yet another fundraising event that encourages wealthy special interests, particularly those seeking lucrative govt contracts, to rub elbows with officials responsible for awarding those contracts.”

… Historian Timothy Snyder: “Whatever turns out to be happening, it is worth recalling (and reporting) that Trump put completely unqualified people in charge of DOD, DHS, and the FBI, and dissolved agencies throughout the govt whose task was cyber defense. He has made us vulnerable in ways that no foreign enemy could achieve.”

On my weekly podcast Uncovered, we talked about the latest on Putin and Trump in China, the Navy Secretary nominee’s disastrous confirmation hearing, Trump’s racist attack on a Black female reporter, Mullin and Duffy’s buffoonery, Bessent throwing Lutnick under the bus, the latest betrayal of Ukraine, Schumer drama, & lots more!

text:
St. Elizabeth of Hungary, Landgravine of Hesse and Thuringia by Father Francis Xavier Weninger, 1876 
.
St. Elizabeth, a model of devotion and purity to those who live singly, a mirror of love and retirement for married people, a most perfect example of patience for widows, and whose virtues deserve to be followed by all, high and low, was born in Hungary. She was a daughter of Andrew II., King of Hungary, and of Gertrude, daughter of the Duke of Carinthia. According to the Roman Breviary, Elizabeth began in early childhood to fear God, and increased in piety with age. The walk she loved best of all was going to church, where she prayed with angelic devotion, and whence it was a difficult task to bring her home, as her greatest delight consisted in praying. At the door of the church, she always took off the jewelled coronet which she wore, and when asked why she did this, she replied: "God forbid that I should ever appear with such a crown before the face of Him who was crowned with thorns, and who, out of love for me, was nailed to the cross." She called Mary, the divine Mother, her mother, and entertained great devotion towards St. John, the Apostle and Evangelist, whom she chose as the special protector of her chastity. She never refused what was asked of her in the name of the Blessed Virgin or in that of St. John. The money allotted to her for her recreation, she gave to the poor, requesting them to say the Ave Maria. She was an enemy to luxury, vain adornments and idleness. Nature had not only bestowed upon her unusual personal beauty, but had also endowed her with great qualities of mind.
.
In obedience to her parents, she gave her hand to Louis, Landgrave of Hesse and Thuringia, and lived with him in continual harmony, her conduct being as blameless in the married state as it had been during her maidenhood. She gave one hour every night to prayer, and spent the day in attendance at the divine service in the church, in devout reading and in working for the poor. She always treated her husband with love and respect, and was a model of all virtues to her subjects. She watched over her domestics with a most careful eye, in order that they might lead a Christian life ; but took always a mother's interest in seeing that their wages were punctually paid. She herself carried to the church the princes and princesses to whom she gave birth; and it was her custom, on these occasions to lay a rich offering on the Altar, and to give abundant alms to the poor. Under her royal robes, she continually wore a garment of hair-cloth.
.
For the sick and the forsaken she had more than a mother's care and solicitude. She erected a hospital in which she nursed the sick and sheltered orphans; besides feeding nine hundred poor people, every day, at the palace, and sending alms to the dwellings of those who were ashamed to beg. She also visited the sick in their houses, and served them most tenderly even when they were leprous. She kissed their hands and feet, and encouraged them to patience. Never did a poor person leave her without receiving alms, and more than once, when she had no money with her, she gave away the veil from her head. She did not hesitate even to mend the clothes of the needy, and during a severe famine, gave all her corn to the sufferers. In one word, she did not neglect anything that Christian charity could do; so that she was universally called the mother of the poor.
.
There were at court many who, on account of her great charity, laughed at and derided her; some even accused her of extravagance. Elizabeth, however, did not allow herself to be diverted from her deeds of kindness, and the Landgrave dismissed her accusers with indignation, probably because he perceived that the more charitable his spouse was, the more he was blessed with temporal goods. Hence he not only abstained from disturbing her in her kind deeds, but assisted her in them as long as he lived. He ended his life in a crusade, in which he joined with several other Christian princes in order to conquer the Holy Land from the infidels. Elizabeth grieved deeply when the news of his death reached her, but submitted to the will of the Almighty, saying: "It is known to Thee, O my God, that I loved no one on this earth more than my husband; not only because he was my husband, but also because he loved Thee with his whole heart. But as it has pleased Thee to call him, I am well contented with Thy holy will; and if I could, against Thy decree, raise him from the dead by reciting one Pater Noster, I would not do it. I only beg of Thee to give him eternal peace, and bestow upon me the grace to serve Thee faithfully until the end of my days." After this heroic submission to the will of God, she caused many masses and prayers to be said for the deceased, gave large alms to the poor, divested herself of her royal robes, and, though but twenty years old, she vowed to live in chaste widowhood for the rest of her days.
.
It pleased the Almighty to try His zealous handmaid most painfully. The nobility made the brother of the deceased Landgrave regent, and accused the holy princess of having impoverished the state by her charity to the poor. Under this pretext, they deprived her of all her possessions, and banished her from the Court, with three children, a son and two daughters. Her former vassals, fearing to draw upon themselves the disfavor of the new government, durst not give her lodgings. Even the hospitals, which she herself had founded, were closed against her. Hence she had to lodge mostly in a stable and to live on the bread she begged. In such unexpected and more than painful circumstances, St. Elizabeth showed a truly heroic, and, to the children of the world, incomprehensible strength and patience. She complained to no one of the injustice of the nobility, not even to her royal father, who was still living; but rejoiced that she could suffer for the love of God. After the first night of her banishment, she went to the Church of the Franciscans and requested them to sing the "Te Deum," or "Great God! we praise thee," to give thanks to God for the sorrows with which He had visited her. 
.
The wrongs and outrages which the holy princess suffered, besides her banishment, can hardly be described. An old woman, who had formerly received clothing and nourishment from St. Elizabeth, dared to push her into a pool of stagnant water, in the street, abusing her at the same time most shamefully, for not having immediately made way for her. This outrage aroused not in the least the wrath of the holy princess; she quietly raised herself out of the pool, cleansed her garments, and offered herself to the Almighty for more suffering. God did not fail to comfort His handmaid in her adversity. Christ appeared to her, during her prayers, encouraged her, and promised never to abandon her. After some time, through her father's influence, a dwelling, suitable to her rank, was conceded to her, and her dowry was refunded. The Saint immediately used one part of the building for a hospital, made her home in the same, and nursed the sick, as if she had been a servant, hired to wait upon them. All her spare time was employed in prayer and other devout exercises. She also chastised her body by fasting and other penances. 
.
At the age of twenty-four years, she learned by revelation, that her end was approaching, for which she prepared herself by most devoutly receiving the holy sacraments. She exhorted all those who were around her death-bed, to love God with their whole heart and to assist the poor to the best of their ability. After this, she continued in prayer, until her soul, richly adorned with virtues and merits, went to her Creator, in the year of Our Lord 1231.
.
PRACTICAL CONSIDERATIONS.
.
I. The life of St. Elizabeth may serve as a model to persons of every age and station. Children may learn to fear God from their earliest years, and to increase their devotion with their age; single persons, how to live chastely in their state; married people, how husband and wife ought to live together; and the widowed how to sanctify their solitude. Masters and mistresses may learn how to take care of their domestics, and pay their wages regularly. Those of a higher station may learn to set a good example to others, and not to be ashamed to appear at public worship. All Christians can find instruction in it, for employing their time well, helping the needy, and bearing crosses and trials sent by heaven. God permitted a Landgravine, a royal princess, to be banished unjustly from court, to beg her bread, and, besides other ignominies, to be refused a shelter among her own subjects. Still she complained not; but, submissive to the decrees of Providence, gave humble thanks for the Almighty for all that He, in His wisdom, had sent her. Even at the death of her husband, what fortitude, what submission to the divine will she manifested! Oh! that all would endeavor, in trials of much less severity, to unite their will with that of God, and patiently bear the cross that He has laid upon them.
.
II. The favorite walk of St. Elizabeth, when she was still a child, was to go to church, where she manifested most angelic devotion, and was so happy, that she could hardly be persuaded to leave. What is your favorite walk? Where do you like to remain? And when you do go to church why are you in such haste to leave it again? Why do you much oftener go to theatres, frivolous societies, vain amusements, bar-rooms and ball-rooms, than to Church, to prayers, to sermons, or to public worship? Why does the sermon, the mass, or conversation with God in prayer so soon become wearisome to you, when many hours, nay, even half the day or night seem not long, when you occupy them in gaming, dancing, or silly conversation? Answer these questions if you can; and then tell me, do you expect to justify yourself before God, and to enter the same heaven into which St. Elizabeth entered? "Ah! truly, heaven becomes not the dwelling of those who sleep and are idle, but of those who earnestly endeavor to gain it." Thus speaks the holy pope, St. Leo.

text:
A Friend of Mine Got Laid Off 23 Days Before His Wedding
​
​On a Friday in November, he got a 15-minute calendar invite from his manager—with an HR rep he’d never met.
​Ten minutes later, he knew he wouldn’t be coming in on Monday.
​He was 32, a senior backend engineer in Bellevue making $185k base ($240k total). The day before, his manager had asked him to watch alerts during the Thanksgiving rush. Now, the product line was dead. HR offered 8 weeks of severance (~$28.5k pre-tax).
​After the call, he opened Slack to say goodbye. It kicked him to the login screen.
​His wedding was 23 days away.
​He and his fiancée had been together five years. The year before, he’d bought a $735k townhouse in Bothell—$4,700/mo all-in. She’d thought it was too steep. He told her his vesting stock would cover it. He could swing it.
​They’d booked a Woodinville winery for 108 guests, with $14,000 already paid.
​He’d even built a Three.js wedding site for the invitation’s QR code—an interactive timeline ending with hundreds of dots forming a heart around their names. She’d posted a screen recording on Instagram: “I asked for a simple website. He took ‘simple’ personally.”
​That Friday night, she asked if he could come home early Monday for the seating chart. He said yes.
​He didn’t show her the severance agreement until Sunday morning.
​“Why didn’t you tell me Friday?”
“I wanted to figure out a plan first.”
“We could’ve figured it out together.”
​Over the next week, he sent 70+ applications, took six recruiter calls, and did two technical interviews. One topped out at $135k base. He said he was still interested.
​He nailed the LRU cache problem in ten minutes. They asked how soon he could start.
​“Next week.”
​Two days later, the recruiter emailed: hiring for the role was on hold.
​With 11 days left, his fiancée called the winery. The final $21,000 was due the next day. Canceling now meant losing the $14,000 deposit and owing nothing more.
​She hung up and turned the seating chart facedown.
​“I want to cancel the wedding.”
​He asked if they could reschedule once he landed a job.
​“When we bought the house, you said you could swing it. You got laid off Friday and told me Sunday. Now you lock yourself in the office all day, and whenever I ask how it’s going, you just say you’re close.”
​She looked up. “I can’t give you another date. I’m scared that even if we get married, we’ll still be dealing with everything alone.”
​That night, they emailed the winery. He called his dad in Ohio twice—the first time to say the wedding was off, the second to ask if the flights were refundable.
​On their wedding day, he opened his laptop. There was one last bug on the site: on some phones, the last letter of her name wrapped onto a new line.
​He fixed it, checked the preview, then logged into the hosting dashboard and took the site down.
​Before closing his laptop, he grabbed a spare invite and scanned the QR code.
​When he was on call, seeing that error meant diving straight into the logs.
​This time, he placed his phone facedown on the desk.

​404 Not Found
