text:
and Grok specifies many vulnerabilities in a simple query...  ie, How Secure are the Dominion, Hart Intercivic, ES&S, and other Voting Systems ?
Grok: They are not specially architecturally hardened at the motherboard or chipset level. Dominion, Hart InterCivic, ES&S, and similar systems primarily use commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware with standard processors, motherboards, and chipsets, rather than custom high-assurance designs resistant to sophisticated hardware attacks.

Hardware Architecture
Dominion (e.g., ImageCast X / Democracy Suite): Explicitly built on COTS components. The ImageCast X ballot-marking device is typically a standard Android tablet (examples in documentation include Samsung Galaxy Tab/Note Pro models or aValue industrial tablets) running Android (sometimes older versions like 5.1 in certified configurations) with a custom voting application layered on top. Scanners (ImageCast Precinct/ICE) use embedded or industrial PC-style hardware with ordinary motherboards and chipsets. Election management systems often run on standard PCs with self-encrypting drives and Microsoft SQL Server.
Hart InterCivic (Verity / Verity Vanguard): Mix of purpose-built enclosures and COTS or semi-custom boards. Newer systems add features such as Secure Boot and allow-listing. Hart’s Verity Vanguard was the first system certified to VVSG 2.0 (in 2025); researchers have described its cybersecurity as “nearly state-of-the-art for consumer-grade devices,” with layered secure boot and better hardening than older systems, but still not military-grade hardware isolation.
Other vendors (ES&S, etc.): Similar pattern—industrial or COTS motherboards, standard chipsets, and peripheral controllers. Older systems sometimes used more specialized embedded controllers.

These are not custom ASICs or extensively isolated hardware roots of trust across the board. Security is layered on top rather than built into the silicon architecture.

Security Model and Standards
U.S. Election Assistance Commission Voluntary Voting System Guidelines (VVSG) govern certification:
Older VVSG 1.0/1.1 systems (still widely used) emphasize software controls, physical port restrictions, logging, and FIPS-validated cryptographic modules more than deep hardware security. Explicit notes in VVSG 2.0 materials clarify there are generally no hardware security module (e.g., TPM) requirements for core functions.
VVSG 2.0 (adopted 2021, first full certifications around 2025) improves things with better cybersecurity requirements: secure configurations, exploit mitigations (ASLR, DEP), cryptographic boot validation, authenticated updates, supply-chain risk management, and stronger physical port controls. It still prioritizes software independence via voter-verifiable paper ballots over pure hardware trustworthiness.

Practical protections include:
Air-gapping or restricted networking during voting.
Kiosk/lockdown modes and restricted ports (some Hart systems use proprietary connectors).
Encryption of election data, redundant storage, and audit logs.
Physical security: locks, tamper-evident seals, chain of custody, and limited access.
Paper ballots (or voter-verified paper audit trails) as the independent record for audits and risk-limiting audits.

Documented Limitations and Vulnerabilities
Independent analyses (California top-to-bottom reviews, Project EVEREST, university researchers such as Alex Halderman’s team, CISA advisories) have repeatedly found issues that are more software/firmware or procedural than pure silicon-level:
Dominion ImageCast X (certain versions): CISA advisory ICSA-22-154-01 documented multiple vulnerabilities (arbitrary code execution via election definition files, weak smartcard authentication, privilege escalation paths, self-attestation weaknesses). Exploitation generally requires physical access, access to the election management system, or the ability to modify files beforehand. CISA stated there was no evidence of exploitation in elections; later software versions addressed many issues.
Older Hart systems: Red-team and source-code reviews found weak or missing cryptography on some links, undocumented functionality, and ease of compromise once physical access was obtained (firmware replacement in seconds in some cases). Newer Verity systems improved this.
Common physical findings across vendors: locks and seals that can be bypassed with moderate effort; cases that open readily once locks are defeated; standard ports or internal access once inside.

Once an attacker has sustained physical access, standard COTS motherboards and chipsets offer limited resistance to advanced techniques (firmware modification, side-channel analysis, etc.), similar to ordinary commercial devices. The intended threat model relies more on preventing or detecting physical access through procedures and seals than on architectural hardware security.

In short, the motherboards and chipsets are ordinary commercial hardware. The systems achieve usable election security through a combination of software controls, operational procedures, physical safeguards, certification testing, and—most importantly—paper ballots that allow independent verification. They are not designed as high-assurance, hardware-isolated platforms resistant to determined physical or supply-chain attacks at the chip level. Newer VVSG 2.0 systems raise the bar, but most deployed equipment still follows the older COTS-plus-procedures model.

text:
❤️ PRAYING FOR JACOB OSORIO
A 17-Year-Old Fighting Cancer — A Mother Carrying the Weight of Love

November 19, 2026

“God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.” — Psalm 46:1 (NIV)

❤️ A YOUNG LIFE INTERRUPTED BY CANCER

In Lowell, Massachusetts, 17-year-old Jacob Osorio is facing a battle no teenager should have to endure.

In January 2026, Jacob was diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma, a cancer affecting the lymphatic system.

His treatment has required frequent hospital visits and stays, bringing emotional strain, financial hardship, and uncertainty into his family's life.

Jacob is the only child of a single mother.

Imagine the weight this mother carries.

She must remain strong for her son while confronting fears that no parent can easily express. Every medical appointment may bring new questions. Every treatment demands endurance. Every unexpected complication can awaken another wave of concern.

And somewhere within this struggle is a 17-year-old young man whose life should be filled with friendships, discoveries, dreams, and anticipation of adulthood.

Cancer has interrupted his adolescence. It has not diminished the value of his life or the future we pray he will experience.

❤️ WHEN LOVE CANNOT REMOVE THE PAIN

One of the most heartbreaking experiences of parenthood is watching a child suffer while being unable to take that suffering away.

A mother can offer her presence, her tenderness, her encouragement, and her prayers.

She cannot command every cancer cell to disappear.

Yet Scripture reveals something extraordinary about the compassion of Jesus Christ.

“Jesus wept.” — John 11:35 (NIV)

Standing before the sorrow surrounding Lazarus, Jesus entered the grief of those He loved.

His tears reveal a Savior whose divine authority never diminishes His compassion.

The suffering of one young man is never too small to matter to the God who knows every human life.

❤️ A COMMUNITY ANSWERS WITH COMPASSION

On November 18, the Lowell Police Department reported that Cops for Kids with Cancer had presented Jacob's family with $5,500 to help relieve the financial burden of his illness.

This generosity reveals an important spiritual truth.

Sometimes compassion arrives through people who refuse to let a struggling family carry everything alone.

A donation cannot guarantee recovery. It can help provide breathing room, practical assistance, and reassurance that someone cares.

When love becomes action, mercy becomes visible.

Galatians 6:2 calls believers to carry one another's burdens.

Jacob's circumstances remind us that prayer and practical generosity belong together.

❤️ OUR PRAYER FOR JACOB

Heavenly Father,

Today we bring Jacob Osorio before Your throne of grace.

You know his body, his diagnosis, his treatments, and every challenge he faces.

Lord Jesus, stretch forth Your healing hand over this young man.

We ask You to destroy the cancer threatening his health, restore his strength, protect his organs, and guide his body toward complete recovery.

Bless his medical team with wisdom, precision, discernment, and compassion.

May every treatment accomplish its intended purpose with the fewest possible complications.

When Jacob feels exhausted, renew his strength.

When fear enters his thoughts, surround him with Your peace.

When tomorrow seems uncertain, fill his heart with courage for today.

Father, give Jacob many healthy years to discover the beauty of the life ahead of him.

❤️ OUR PRAYER FOR HIS MOTHER

Merciful Father,

We lift up Jacob's mother, whose love carries responsibilities that cannot be measured in money or hours.

You see the sacrifices she makes and the worries she may never speak aloud.

Provide for her financial needs.

Give her restful sleep, wise medical guidance, dependable friendships, and people who recognize when she needs help.

Protect her from exhaustion and despair.

Remind her that receiving assistance is not weakness. Love was never intended to carry every burden alone.

May she experience the tenderness of Your presence throughout this difficult journey.

❤️ OUR PRAYER FOR EVERY FAMILY FACING CHILDHOOD CANCER

Lord, we remember the countless children undergoing chemotherapy, the parents sleeping beside hospital beds, and the families struggling with expenses and uncertainty.

Bring healing where bodies are suffering.

Bring comfort where hearts are breaking.

Bring provision where resources are disappearing.

Raise up compassionate physicians, generous communities, faithful friends, and courageous caregivers.

Let hope find its way into hospital rooms.

Let laughter return to frightened households.

Let children experience the ordinary joys of growing up.

And may every family discover that their suffering has not escaped Your loving attention.

In the mighty and compassionate name of Jesus Christ,

Amen. ❤️

“Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.” — 1 Peter 5:7 (NIV)

❤️ Today, let us remember Jacob Osorio and his mother. One family's suffering deserves more than a passing thought. It deserves our compassion, our prayers, and wherever possible, our practical love.

$KEYS KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM KEYSIGHT TECHNOLOGIES’ FISCAL Q4 2026 EARNINGS CALL

Keysight’s November 19 results provide strong cross-industry evidence that AI infrastructure investment is translating into manufacturing capacity, component qualification, and increasingly complex system validation. Orders increased 53%, core revenue increased 36%, and annual AI bookings reached approximately 2.5x the prior-year level. The most actionable implications extend beyond generic AI exposure: photonics testing can generate revenue before widespread co-packaged-optics deployment; existing optical modules retain a substantial production runway; and increasingly heterogeneous networks expand opportunities for merchant silicon and interconnect suppliers. The principal negative implications concern cash investment, nonrecurring earnings benefits, and overly aggressive commercialization assumptions, rather than demonstrated deterioration in underlying demand. Most relevant peers have already reported October or November results, making this call an additional supply-chain confirmation rather than evidence of undisclosed awards or automatic earnings beats. Magnitude assessments below distinguish business-level exposure from consolidated earnings significance. Country labels indicate corporate domicile; Fabrinet’s principal manufacturing base is in Thailand.

PHOTONICS TESTING: REVENUE CAN PRECEDE THE CPO DEPLOYMENT INFLECTION (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected company: FormFactor (FORM: United States). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High strategic importance for its photonics systems business, but initially modest consolidated financial impact.

The strongest differentiated read-through is that optical test infrastructure can monetize the transition before co-packaged optics becomes a large installed-system market. Keysight stated that leading foundries are taking silicon photonics into commercial production and that these programs “require optical validation alongside electrical parametric tests we already provide.” Separately, management placed the larger NPO/CPO inflection in 2028. These statements are compatible: production processes, qualification equipment, and wafer-level screening must be established before large downstream deployments.

The transmission mechanism is the increasing importance of identifying known-good photonic dies before they are combined with electronic dies and expensive packaging. Optical alignment, coupling efficiency, electrical performance, and wafer-level repeatability require specialized equipment. Testing earlier in the manufacturing process reduces the risk of discovering a defective optical component after substantial assembly value has been added. This creates equipment demand ahead of final-system shipments.

FormFactor’s October 28 call provides direct corroboration. Its Systems business grew 20% sequentially, and management increased its 2026 TRITON revenue expectation from an initial $10 million-$20 million to more than $30 million. It also explicitly identified exposure to CPO, NPO, and pluggable devices. The opportunity is therefore not dependent on a single optical architecture winning immediately.

The important magnitude distinction is that rapid photonics growth does not yet justify treating FormFactor as a predominantly photonics company. The disclosed TRITON contribution remains relatively small against consolidated quarterly revenue of $280.5 million. Its significance is the emergence of another production-test platform with potential follow-on equipment and probe demand, not an immediate transformation of consolidated earnings.

Near-term catalyst: Q4 2026 results and 2027 commentary on optical-system orders, customer qualifications, and shipments. Keysight’s call strengthens confidence in the spending environment but does not establish an additional FormFactor order.

Longer-duration implication: Through 2027-2028, wafer-level optical testing should benefit from commercialization across several architectures. This is a shared-market read-through, not a claim that Keysight’s orders pass through to FormFactor or that the companies have identical competitive positions.

OPTICAL MODULES: THE 800G/1.6T PRODUCTION CYCLE HAS MORE IMMEDIATE SUPPORT THAN CPO DISPLACEMENT (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected companies: Fabrinet (FN: Cayman Islands), Coherent (COHR: United States), and Lumentum Holdings (LITE: United States). Direction: Positive for existing optical production; negative for assumptions that CPO rapidly displaces that business during 2027. Magnitude: Potentially substantial for exposed optical businesses, with the clearest manufacturing transmission at Fabrinet.

Keysight reported that transceiver and module manufacturers were scaling production of 800G and 1.6T modules using its digital communication analyzers. Wireline revenue grew at a triple-digit rate, with strong activity in both R&D and manufacturing. Production-test investment is more directly relevant to near-term module shipments than research demonstrations alone because it indicates customers are preparing to qualify and manufacture output at higher volumes.

For Fabrinet, the mechanism is additional optical assembly, alignment, packaging, and production capacity serving customer programs. For Coherent and Lumentum, the mechanism includes demand for optical components and modules used in faster links. Revenue depends on qualified programs, shipped units, supplier content, and realized prices, rather than on the growth rate of Keysight’s instruments.

The timing distinction is important. Dhanasekaran said the NPO/CPO transition was underway but that “we think it is largely a bigger inflection in 2028.” That supports continued coexistence of pluggables, near-packaged optics, and co-packaged optics rather than an immediate replacement cycle. Fabrinet’s November 2 call similarly described NPO/CPO contributions toward the latter part of fiscal 2027, while emphasizing that these opportunities complement its pluggable business.

This is not a bearish conclusion on CPO suppliers. Lumentum had already disclosed a major NPO/CPO win backed by purchase commitments exceeding $5 billion. Keysight’s commentary does not invalidate that commitment or establish a delay against Lumentum’s delivery schedule. It does argue against treating multiyear commitments, initial production, and broad industry deployment as interchangeable revenue milestones.

The more defensible relative conclusion favors businesses with current optical shipments and multiple architecture exposures over valuations dependent predominantly on an assumed immediate CPO inflection. Lumentum’s other drivers, including optical circuit switches and pump lasers, also mean that pluggable-module commentary cannot explain its entire earnings trajectory.

Near-term catalyst: December-quarter shipment, utilization, and guidance updates following the peers’ already-reported November results. The call provides incremental confidence in production demand, not proof that any particular company will beat its existing forecast.

Longer-duration implication: Optical bandwidth growth can support multiple architectures simultaneously. The principal risk is not simply technological substitution; it is whether new capacity, yields, and product mix generate acceptable returns as architectures evolve.

OPTICAL MANUFACTURING: CAPACITY EXPANSION IS A MATERIAL CASH-FLOW HEADWIND EVEN WHEN DEMAND IS STRONG (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected company: Fabrinet (FN: Cayman Islands). Direction: Negative for near-term free-cash-flow conversion, while positive for potential future production capacity. Magnitude: Material at the consolidated cash-flow level.

Keysight’s supply discussion indicates that demand fulfillment increasingly requires physical investment rather than only better utilization of existing facilities. Management described an approximately 18-month supply-planning horizon, continuing manufacturing expansion, and fiscal 2027 capital expenditures of approximately $275 million. Demand still exceeded shipment capability despite repeated capacity increases.

The cross-company implication is that strong AI bookings should not automatically be valued as immediately distributable earnings. Capacity additions require buildings, equipment, qualification work, and working capital before they generate mature production economics. Customers’ demands for faster ramps can accelerate these cash outflows.

Fabrinet’s November 2 disclosures illustrate the mechanism directly. Operating cash flow was approximately $21 million, capital expenditures were approximately $159 million, and reported free cash flow was an outflow of approximately $137 million. Capital spending included a $77 million Santa Clara campus purchase alongside other expansion projects. Removing that property purchase alone would still leave approximately $60 million of cash outflow, although that calculation is not a fully normalized free-cash-flow measure because other growth investment and working-capital effects remain.

This is a cash-conversion caution, not evidence that Fabrinet’s demand is weakening. Management described strong existing programs, new optical opportunities, and substantial additional capacity. The investment issue is the timing and risk of turning that expenditure into revenue and cash. Capacity expressed in revenue terms is not itself booked sales, and successful construction does not establish customer qualification, utilization, or final returns.

Near-term catalyst: The next quarterly cash-flow disclosure, including working-capital absorption, capital spending, and progress toward customer-qualified output. An earnings beat accompanied by continued cash outflows would have a different valuation implication from an earnings beat with improving conversion.

Longer-duration implication: Capacity that fills efficiently can support sustained growth. Capacity commissioned into slower demand can depress utilization and returns. The appropriate distinction is between temporarily investment-heavy growth and permanently weaker cash economics, not between strong orders and weak orders alone.

AI NETWORKING: HETEROGENEITY EXPANDS MERCHANT SILICON AND DISTRIBUTED-NETWORK OPPORTUNITIES (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected companies: Broadcom (AVGO: United States) and Cisco Systems (CSCO: United States). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: Meaningful for AI networking businesses; potentially material to consolidated growth, but not quantifiable from Keysight’s disclosures alone.

Keysight described AI infrastructure as becoming more heterogeneous across processors, interconnects, protocols, and suppliers. It specifically cited collaboration with Broadcom on a multivendor Ethernet scale-up interoperability demonstration and with Cisco on scale-across networks. These are identifiable relationships rather than generic associations with AI spending.

For Broadcom, the transmission mechanism is broader adoption of merchant Ethernet switching in demanding accelerator fabrics. Keysight’s October OCP announcement identified demonstrations involving Tomahawk 6 and Tomahawk Ultra, including link-layer retry and credit-based flow control. These functions address reliable transport and congestion management, helping Ethernet operate in environments where communication failures can impair expensive accelerator utilization.

Successful interoperability reduces technical adoption risk and supports a larger addressable deployment opportunity. It does not establish a specific customer’s production allocation or prove displacement of competing accelerator-interconnect architectures. The strongest conclusion is that the merchant ecosystem is becoming more capable and commercially relevant.

Cisco’s mechanism is different. Scale-across architectures connect distributed computing capacity and therefore require routing, buffering, coherent optics, and system-level coordination, not just additional switches inside a single facility. Cisco’s October 12 disclosure described Silicon One P200-based systems, deep-buffered routing, and coherent optics, with production deployments at named hyperscalers. Keysight’s workload-emulation commentary reinforces the importance of validating the entire packet-to-optical path under coordinated AI workloads.

Near-term catalyst: Broadcom’s scheduled December 9 earnings release and outlook. Keysight provides a relevant demand cross-check before that event, but test-equipment bookings cannot be converted directly into a Broadcom revenue forecast. Cisco’s November 12 results have already occurred, so the read-through concerns subsequent conversion and guidance rather than an upcoming Q1 report.

Longer-duration implication: Through 2027-2028, architectural diversity can expand merchant silicon and distributed-network content. The competitive benefit is increased customer choice and a larger range of deployable solutions, not evidence that any single proprietary ecosystem has already lost its position.

ELECTRONIC COMPONENTS: AI DEMAND IS MOVING BELOW THE TRANSCEIVER INTO PCBS AND PASSIVES (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected companies: TTM Technologies (TTMI: United States) and Murata Manufacturing (6981: Japan). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: Material for TTM’s data-center and networking exposure; meaningful for Murata’s capacitor business, with more diluted consolidated sensitivity.

Keysight reported continued demand from PCB manufacturers adding high-frequency test capacity. It also said component-test demand was gaining traction in multilayer ceramic capacitors and photodiodes. This is a more specific signal than a broad claim that all electronic components benefit equally from AI.

For TTM, higher-speed boards and more demanding signal-integrity requirements increase the importance of manufacturing precision, materials selection, process control, and electrical validation. The economic opportunity is not simply more PCB units. It includes a shift toward more technically demanding products where qualification barriers and manufacturing execution can matter more than commodity pricing.

TTM’s October 22 results establish meaningful exposure: data-center and networking applications represented 41% of quarterly sales, while aerospace and defense represented 34%. Keysight’s commentary therefore supports a substantial existing business rather than a peripheral prospective application. It does not, however, establish TTM’s specific customer allocation or justify transferring Keysight’s growth rate to TTM.

For Murata, the mechanism is increasing demand for capacitors that support power integrity and reliable operation in dense, high-performance systems. More demanding qualification and test requirements support the relevance of high-performance products and controlled manufacturing processes. They do not independently prove higher capacitor counts per system, stronger selling prices, or a particular supplier’s share gain.

Murata’s October 30 announcement provides a direct capacity response: approximately ¥1 trillion of planned MLCC investment across fiscal 2026-2030, including roughly ¥650 billion of production equipment. The plan targets at least 2x fiscal 2025 MLCC sales by fiscal 2030. Keysight’s component-test commentary corroborates the engineering demands underlying that investment, but does not guarantee the sales target.

Near-term catalyst: Subsequent disclosures on data-center mix, production yields, utilization, and customer qualification. For Murata, evidence that growth comes from higher-value products rather than precautionary ordering would be especially useful.

Longer-duration implication: AI infrastructure can raise the value of specialized components previously grouped with broad electronics exposure. The cross-portfolio caution is that owning PCBs, capacitors, optical modules, and networking silicon does not create independent demand diversification when all depend increasingly on the same infrastructure budgets.

TEST-EQUIPMENT EARNINGS: TARIFF REFUNDS AND COST CLASSIFICATION CAN OVERSTATE RECURRING IMPROVEMENT (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected company: FormFactor (FORM: United States). Direction: Negative for mechanical extrapolation of reported adjusted earnings; not a negative demand signal. Magnitude: Moderate for quarterly earnings comparability and potentially important for valuation.

Keysight disclosed that fiscal 2026 gross margin included a nonrecurring 110-basis-point benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds and explicitly excluded that tailwind from its fiscal 2027 outlook. The relevant peer implication is not that every test-equipment company received the same benefit. It is that strong reported operating leverage must be checked against company-specific discrete items before being treated as recurring.

FormFactor’s October 28 call provides the required company-specific evidence. Management attributed approximately $0.09 of Q3 adjusted EPS to tariff refunds. Against reported adjusted EPS of $1.04, the refund represented approximately 8.7%. Removing that item alone produces approximately $0.95 of adjusted EPS, without claiming that every other adjustment has been normalized.

The transmission mechanism is straightforward: a refund improves the current earnings base without requiring an equivalent increase in sustainable production economics. When the benefit does not recur, underlying growth must replace it before reported earnings can continue rising at the same apparent rate. This is a comparison headwind, not an automatic forecast cut, particularly in a business with strong demand.

There is also an important counterpoint for interpreting FormFactor’s factory ramp. Management said approximately $5 million of startup costs would move from operating expenses into cost of revenues in Q4. At the $285 million revenue midpoint, that classification change is equivalent to approximately 175 basis points of gross margin. It does not, by itself, reduce operating profit because the cost is being reclassified rather than newly created.

Near-term catalyst: Q4 results and 2027 margin guidance. The relevant comparison separates tariff benefits, recurring operating performance, startup expenditure, and expense classification. A lower reported gross margin could coexist with stable operating economics, while a high adjusted EPS figure could include a nonrecurring benefit.

Longer-duration implication: The market should distinguish durable test intensity and manufacturing efficiencies from temporary accounting or cash-recovery effects. Keysight’s own normalization makes that discipline more important across the sector, not less.

WIRELESS TESTING: 6G DEVELOPMENT SPENDING CAN RECOVER BEFORE A CARRIER DEPLOYMENT CYCLE (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected company: Anritsu (6754: Japan). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: Moderate potential company-level benefit over time; limited evidence for an immediate consolidated earnings step-change attributable specifically to 6G.

Keysight reported double-digit wireless order growth and said its 6G business doubled year-over-year. The more consequential commentary was that leading chipset and network-equipment companies were moving from research into funded development. Management maintained the 2029 Release 21 milestone and highlighted technology preparation for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The transmission mechanism favors test vendors earlier than many downstream network suppliers. Chipset and equipment developers need measurement, simulation, interoperability, and certification capabilities before operators deploy commercial networks. Spending on those tools can therefore increase while carrier capital expenditure and commercial 6G revenue remain limited.

Anritsu’s October 29 presentation independently anticipated full-fledged demand for 6G test instruments beginning around 2027 and identified earlier demand for FR3-related development associated with the 2028 showcase. This supports a specific timing opportunity rather than an undated technology theme.

The magnitude should nevertheless be constrained by the company’s actual mix. Test and measurement represented approximately 61% of Anritsu’s first-half revenue, and mobile represented approximately 27% of that segment, equivalent to roughly 16% of group revenue. Current 6G activity is only a subset of mobile. It is therefore inappropriate to apply Keysight’s 6G growth rate to Anritsu’s consolidated business.

Counterevidence also matters. Anritsu continued to describe traditional 5G development investment as sluggish. Its recent profitability improvement was driven substantially by optical-transceiver manufacturing solutions, and its Q&A acknowledged that some earlier orders had been brought forward at customer request. Those disclosures argue against interpreting strong test demand as a uniform wireless recovery.

Near-term catalyst: Evidence in subsequent order and guidance updates that funded 6G and NTN development is becoming a material mobile-test contributor. The immediate opportunity is stronger development spending, not an assumed near-term surge in commercial network installations.

Longer-duration implication: The 2027-2029 development window can provide another demand source alongside optical infrastructure. The call does not establish a broad recovery in smartphones, conventional 5G investment, or telecommunications-operator spending.

DEFENSE ELECTRONICS: SPECTRUM OPERATIONS AND RADAR HAVE A MORE DIRECT TRANSMISSION THAN DEFENSE BUDGETS GENERALLY (READ-THROUGH 8)

Affected companies: HENSOLDT (HAG: Germany) and L3Harris Technologies (LHX: United States). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High strategic relevance and meaningful potential financial impact for HENSOLDT’s concentrated sensor exposure; moderate consolidated read-through for the more diversified L3Harris.

Keysight reported record aerospace, defense, and government bookings, with strong double-digit order growth across regions. Management described defense budgets translating into “new programs and production,” and identified electromagnetic spectrum operations as a particular strength. Threat emulation, radar, counter-UAV detection, and resilience against GPS disruption were recurring applications.

The precise transmission is through engineering validation and production capacity for more demanding electronic systems. New radar waveforms, electronic-attack capabilities, autonomous threats, and contested navigation environments require simulation and testing before equipment can be accepted or produced at scale. That makes Keysight’s evidence more directly relevant to sensor and electronic-warfare suppliers than to every company benefiting from higher defense budgets.

HENSOLDT’s November 5 disclosures provide a particularly close exposure match. Sensors order intake increased 54.5%, supported by radar programs, electronic-attack prototypes, and additional air-defense radar orders. European sovereign-capability investment therefore has a demonstrated commercial channel into the company, rather than being solely a policy narrative.

L3Harris also has directly relevant programs. Its October 29 release identified an $876 million modification for the U.S. Navy’s Next Generation Jammer Low Band program and a 1.9x book-to-bill ratio in Communications & Spectrum Dominance. These are more relevant comparisons than its total backlog, which also contains substantial missile-propulsion awards with different demand drivers.

Keysight did not identify the U.S. prime contractor behind its new threat-emulation selection. That award cannot be assigned to L3Harris, and the Navy reference does not establish that the companies participate in the same specific contract. The positive conclusion rests on independently verified exposure to the same spending categories.

Near-term catalyst: Conversion of funded programs into deliveries, acceptance milestones, and updated production guidance. HENSOLDT’s scheduled February 24, 2027 results provide a defined checkpoint. Keysight’s own defense revenue grew only approximately 7% despite much stronger orders, demonstrating that procurement activity and recognized revenue can diverge materially.

Longer-duration implication: Through 2027 and beyond, electronic warfare, radar modernization, and counter-UAV systems support a durable upgrade cycle across U.S. and European markets. This offers more distinct budget exposure than another AI infrastructure holding, although program timing, manufacturing execution, contract structure, and customer acceptance still determine earnings and cash realization.

🌍 WORLD MILITARY FILES
🇺🇸 ARLEIGH BURKE CLASS — AMERICA'S AEGIS DESTROYER

⚓ More than 30 knots. Up to 96 vertical launch cells on modern variants. Advanced radar and missile-defense capabilities.

Meet the Arleigh Burke class, one of the most important warship classes in the U.S. Navy.

The first ship entered service in 1991.

More than 35 years later, America is still building improved versions.

Why?

Let's explore.

🔹 1. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

Focusing on the modern Flight III configuration:

• Length: 155.3 meters (509.5 ft)
• Beam: Approximately 18 meters (59 ft)
• Displacement: Approximately 9,700 long tons
• Speed: Over 30 knots
• Propulsion: 4 LM2500 gas turbines
• Crew: Approximately 359
• Vertical launch system: 96 cells
• Helicopter facilities: Up to 2 MH-60 helicopters

Figures are based on published U.S. Navy specifications. Actual equipment and displacement can vary between ships and configurations.

🔹 2. WHAT IS THE AEGIS COMBAT SYSTEM?

The ship's real strength goes beyond its missiles.

Aegis integrates radar, computers, command systems and weapons to detect, track and engage threats.

Instead of treating every weapon as a separate system, Aegis coordinates multiple defensive and offensive capabilities.

Depending on ship configuration, it supports operations against aircraft, cruise missiles and ballistic missile threats.

But Aegis is not an impenetrable shield.

Its effectiveness depends on sensors, weapons, target characteristics and operational conditions.

🔹 3. 96 VERTICAL LAUNCH CELLS

One of the destroyer's most important features is the Mk 41 Vertical Launching System.

Modern Flight IIA and Flight III ships generally have 96 launch cells.

These can accommodate different compatible weapons, including:

🚀 Standard Missiles — Air and missile defense
🎯 Tomahawk — Long-range land attack
🌊 VL-ASROC — Anti-submarine warfare
🛡️ ESSM — Ship and fleet air defense

Important distinction:

96 launch cells do NOT necessarily mean 96 missiles.

Some compatible interceptors can be packed more than one per cell, while the actual weapon mix varies by mission.

🔹 4. THE BIG UPGRADE: FLIGHT III

Flight III introduces the AN/SPY-6(V)1 Air and Missile Defense Radar.

According to RTX, its configuration includes:

📡 4 fixed radar array faces
📡 37 radar modular assemblies per face
📡 Continuous 360-degree situational awareness

The radar offers improved sensitivity and detection capabilities compared with its predecessor.

Flight III also incorporates upgrades to electrical power and cooling systems.

That's essential because powerful sensors and combat computers require substantial energy and thermal management.

🔹 5. MORE THAN AIR DEFENSE

Arleigh Burke-class destroyers are multirole warships.

Their missions include:

✈️ Air and missile defense
🚢 Anti-surface warfare
🌊 Anti-submarine warfare
🎯 Land-attack operations
⚓ Carrier strike group protection

Modern variants can operate MH-60 helicopters for missions including anti-submarine warfare and maritime surveillance.

The ship also carries a 5-inch naval gun and other defensive weapons.

🔹 6. WHY ARE THESE SHIPS SO IMPORTANT?

Aircraft carriers provide mobile airpower, but they require protection against multiple threats.

Destroyers can contribute radar coverage, missile defense, anti-submarine capabilities and additional strike options.

They can also operate independently.

In other words, a destroyer is much more than a smaller warship protecting an aircraft carrier.

It's a powerful combat platform in its own right.

🔹 7. LATEST NEWS: A NEW FLIGHT III DESTROYER

In the occult system of Aleister Crowley, moving "forward in reverse" refers to the mandatory training of the magician to think, speak, write, and act backwards. Detailed in his work Liber ThIShARB (Liber 913) and later collected in Magick: Book 4, this process is designed to break down conventional frameworks of time and perception. 

The Law of Reversal
Crowley posited that to perceive the past, understand karma, or discover one's "True Will," an adept must master the Occult Law of Reversal. By forcing the mind to process reality in reverse, the practitioner aims to unlock hidden layers of memory and subconscious power. [1, 2]
According to Crowley’s specific instructions, an adept must train using the following methods:
Writing Backwards: Learning to write text in reverse, using either hand. 
Walking Backwards: Moving physically in reverse to disrupt muscle memory and spatial habit. 
Listening Backwards: Listening to phonograph records or audio clips played in reverse (a practice that later heavily influenced the concept of "backmasking" in music).
Speaking Backwards: Reversing phonetics out loud (e.g., transforming the phrase "I am He" into "Eh ma I"). [1]
Reversed Thinking: Seating oneself in meditation and mentally tracing the day's events perfectly backward, from the current moment down to the exact second of waking up.

Purpose and Cultural Legacy
Magical Aim: Crowley designed these techniques to shatter the psychological illusion of linear time and habitual ego-thought, assisting the magician in cultivating the "Magical Memory" (including past-life recall) and surviving profound spiritual states.
Backmasking Influence: Crowley’s recommendation to listen to reversed audio records later became a foundational reference point for the 20th-century concept of backmasking in rock and heavy metal music (such as allegations involving Led Zeppelin or the Beatles).

The three stages of alchemy
The Nigredo is the first of the three main stages the alchemical work must pass through to achieve what’s known as the philosopher’s stone. At the practical level, the philosopher’s stone is represented by gold, the purest of metals; psychologically, the stone is akin to the birth of the true, authentic self; and spiritually, we’re basically talking about enlightenment.

In brief, the three stages go like this (please don’t worry about retaining everything here because I’ll return to the parts you need to know):

First, the Nigredo, or blackening, in which the base matter is heated to burn away the unnecessary and bring impurities to light. Nigredo symbolism includes the Black Dragon, ravens or crows, bones and decaying bodies, and the Black Sun (or sol niger).

Next, the Albedo, or whitening, in which the matter is separated, distilled, and purified; its essence extracted and released. Albedo symbols include the white swan or dove, the moon, clear water, and the White Queen.

There is a transitional stage next, known as the Citrinitas or the yellowing, which involves the infusion of warmth and spiritual insight, symbolised by honey, ripening wheat, and the sun rising on the new day.

The Rubedo, or the reddening – the final stage of the work – involves the integration of opposites and the experience of the true self, culminating in the Philosopher’s Stone, the perfected work across all three planes: material gold, psychological wholeness, and spiritual enlightenment.

The symbols for this stage include the phoenix, the full sun, the Red King, and the hermaphrodite (or rebis) – which represents the integrated whole, where masculine and feminine are united.

The word rubio comes from the Latin word rubeus, which means "red". [1]

Etymology and Meaning Evolution
Latin Origin: It derives from rubeus (red or reddish, like a blackberry before it ripens).
Shift in Spanish: Over time in Spanish, the meaning shifted from "red" to describe golden, yellowish, or fair hair and complexions (blond). It historically started as a nickname for someone with red hair, a red beard, or a ruddy complexion before generalizing to fair-haired individuals.
Catalan Variant: In Catalan (Rubió), it can also function as a habitational name taken from places named Rubió in Catalonia.

Red giants are evolved from main-sequence stars with masses in the range from about 0.3 M☉ to around 8 M☉.[13] When a star initially forms from a collapsing molecular cloud in the interstellar medium, it contains primarily hydrogen and helium, with trace amounts of "metals" (in astrophysics, this refers to all elements other than hydrogen and helium). These elements are all uniformly mixed throughout the star. The star "enters" the main sequence when its core reaches a temperature (several million kelvins) high enough to begin fusing hydrogen-1 (the predominant isotope), and establishes hydrostatic equilibrium. (In astrophysics, stellar fusion is often referred to as "burning", with hydrogen fusion sometimes termed "hydrogen burning".) Over its main sequence life, the star slowly fuses the hydrogen in the core into helium; its main-sequence life ends when nearly all the hydrogen in the core has been fused. For the Sun, the main-sequence lifetime is approximately 10 billion years. More massive stars burn their fuel disproportionately faster and so have a shorter lifetime than less massive stars.

text:
David Robinson was the league’s MVP.

Against Hakeem Olajuwon in the 1995 Western Conference Finals, even that distinction offered no protection.

Robinson had the size, speed and defensive instincts to ruin an opponent’s night. That is what makes this series extraordinary. Hakeem was doing this to someone equipped to stop almost anybody.

Across six games, Olajuwon averaged 35.3 points, 12.5 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 4.2 blocks, shooting 56 percent from the field.

Houston won the series in six.

The numbers establish the dominance. The footwork explains the helplessness.

Hakeem could show a defender a shot worth contesting, then use that reaction to create a better one. His shoulders sold one direction. His feet preserved another. He could pivot away from pressure without surrendering his balance or the ability to finish.

A defender’s correct first reaction could become the opening for Hakeem’s next move.

That is the cruelty of a complete offensive repertoire. Stay down and he could shoot over you. Commit to the contest and he could step through. Lean toward the baseline and he could turn back into the middle.

The moves worked together because each threat was credible.

In Game 2, he scored 41 points. The reigning champion was making the newly crowned MVP solve problems that kept changing after the possession had begun.

None of this makes Robinson’s award undeserved. A regular season MVP recognizes a season, and Robinson had earned his standing.

It makes Hakeem’s performance more impressive.

Reducing Robinson to a punchline removes the very thing that gives this series its weight. An extraordinary defender met an extraordinary scorer operating at the height of his powers.

Robinson could take away an option.

Hakeem kept having another.

● #FurDay

November 20 is Fur Day. It is a fitting observance for the season when we start longing for a warm coat collar. Its date hides a clever bit of wordplay that weaves in an English word.

The day was established in 1989 by the #JapanFurAssociation (JFA), a general incorporated association headquartered in #NihonbashiKabutochoChuoTokyo. The date comes from a pun: 11 is read as "ii" (good), 2 as "fu," and 0, shaped like a ring, as a stretched "aa," together forming "ii faa," or "good fur." It began as part of a campaign to promote demand for fur. As an organization of fur specialists, the association conducts research on the industry, collects and provides information, and also holds the #JFAFurDesignContest and offers fur appraisals.

Fur refers to animal hide with the hair still attached. Genuine animal fur is called #RealFur, while materials that use no animal fur are known as #FakeFur; today, the hide is generally tanned before use. Humans are thought to have used fur from hunted animals as clothing since the #Paleolithic era. In Japan, too, fur has been found at ancient Paleolithic sites, and the animals used over the ages are remarkably varied, including brown bears, foxes, martens, mink, chinchillas, sea otters, and beavers.

Today, take out that fur-trimmed coat sleeping at the back of your closet. Simply airing it in a well-ventilated, shady spot and brushing it with a soft brush will get you ready for the heart of winter. Real or faux, wearing a single garment with care for years is itself a form of respect for the material. Our talk of warmth now takes a small detour, to the dinner tables of #Italy.

.@HyundaiIndia has unveiled the eighth-generation Elantra at the LA Auto Show. Sold as the Avante in Korea, the sedan grows to 4,795 mm in length (+85 mm), 1,855 mm in width (+30 mm) and 2,750 mm in wheelbase (+30 mm). Rear legroom rises by 29 mm to 993 mm. Styling follows the Art of Steel design language, with H-Edge lighting at the front and rear.

Two powertrains are offered. The 1.6L hybrid makes 157 PS combined and uses a six-speed dual-clutch gearbox. The 2.0L petrol makes 149 PS with an IVT and is rated at 35 mpg. Hybrid fuel economy is still under EPA certification. Inside, a 12.9-inch Pleos Connect screen runs Android Automotive OS with OTA updates and the Gleo AI assistant, while key controls stay as physical buttons.

The Avante launched in Korea in August 2026. The Elantra reaches global markets, including North America, in early 2027. Pricing has not been announced, and there is no word yet on India.

November 20, 2026 | Overnight Dispatch Update Through 12:01am 

JEFFERSON COUNTY, LAKEWOOD AND WHEAT RIDGE

11:41 PM | Unsafe Driver Reported on C-470 Near Wadsworth

A caller reported a gray Toyota Sienna traveling westbound on C-470 near Wadsworth Boulevard, failing to maintain its lane and driving erratically. The reporting party remained in contact with dispatch and was willing to assist.

10:58 PM | Police Search for Suspects in Stolen Vehicle Case

Police established a perimeter near Fenton Street and Gray Street in Wheat Ridge while searching for suspects reportedly connected to a stolen vehicle and felony eluding investigation. Officers checked a possible sighting in a backyard near the 2600 block of Fenton Street, but the suspected person was later determined to be shadows.

10:56 PM | K9 Search Requested in Stolen Vehicle Investigation

Additional radio traffic from the Wheat Ridge area described officers locating a stolen vehicle and searching for one or possibly two suspects near Fenton Street. Officers reported possible movement behind a backyard shed, secured the area and prepared a K9 search. No arrests were confirmed in the available reports.

10:41 PM | Stolen Truck Located, Driver Sought in Edgewater

Officers in the Edgewater and Lakewood area searched near Harlan Street after a reported stolen vehicle and felony eluding incident. Police located the vehicle with its passenger door open, established a perimeter and requested aerial and K9 assistance. A suspect was reportedly last seen near a yard close to a creek or river area.

10:38 PM | Outside Fire Near James Lake Park in Lakewood

West Metro Fire Rescue responded to a reported outside fire near West 13th Avenue and Estes Street. The location was later updated to an area closer to James Lake Park, north of the railroad tracks.

10:36 PM | Possible Overdose in Golden

Jefferson County fire and medical units were requested to stage near West 4th Avenue in Golden after police reported a possible overdose. Additional information about the patient’s condition was unavailable.

10:38 PM | Injury Crash on West 104th Avenue

Emergency dispatch reported a possible injury crash along West 104th Avenue in Northglenn. No additional information about the vehicles or injuries was available.

9:15 PM | Structure Fire at Westminster Country Club

Firefighters responded to a working structure fire at Westminster Country Club on Country Club Drive. Crews reported fire extending into the attic above the second floor. Firefighters established a water supply, completed a primary search, accessed hot spots and began overhaul operations. Gas was secured, utilities were requested and a fire investigator was called.

WESTMINSTER AND NORTH METRO AREA

11:43 PM | Possible Overdose on West 116th Avenue

Emergency crews discussed a possible overdose near West 116th Avenue in Westminster. One responding unit reported carrying a cyanide kit to meet another responder. The circumstances and patient’s condition were not confirmed.

11:41 PM | Wrong-Way Driver Reported on Highway 85

Dispatch received a report of a tan or dark-colored Honda CR-V traveling southbound in the northbound lanes of Highway 85 near Titan Parkway. The vehicle was reportedly traveling at high speed and failing to maintain its lane.

BOULDER COUNTY

11:47 PM | Traffic Control Requested on US 36

Emergency crews requested traffic control near the Baseline Road on-ramp to eastbound US 36 in Boulder. Vehicles were reportedly approaching at high speeds, creating a possible hazard for responders.

11:22 PM | Strong Gas Odor Near Boulder Theater

Boulder fire crews responded to a reported strong gas odor near 14th Street and Spruce Street, approximately half a block north of the Boulder Theater. The odor was reported on the west side of the street.

11:10 PM | Burglary Alarm at Louisville Bagel Shop

Deputies were dispatched to a bagel shop on Courtesy Road in Louisville after a front door entry sensor activated. A deputy noticed a delivery truck outside and planned to inspect the business. A burglary was not confirmed.

10:44 PM | Family Disturbance in Erie

Officers responded to a reported domestic disturbance near Sandstone Circle in Erie involving a 30-year-old woman described as intoxicated. The incident had reportedly been physical earlier, but family members were being separated when dispatch received an update. No weapons were believed to be involved.

DENVER

12:01 AM, NOVEMBER 20 | Possibly Abandoned Bus at 48th and Washington

An officer was requested to check the area near East 48th Avenue and Washington Street after transit police reported a possibly abandoned bus.

11:56 PM | Disruptive Passenger at Decatur-Federal Station

Transit personnel reported a woman refusing to leave a train near Decatur-Federal Station. The passenger reportedly boarded again after being removed and remained on the platform, possibly attempting to board other trains or climb onto an approaching train’s coupler.

11:23 PM | Fire in Grocery Cart at Lawrence and Broadway

Denver firefighters were dispatched to Lawrence Street and Broadway after a fire was reported inside a large grocery cart containing clothing and trash. The cart had reportedly been at the location throughout the day.

11:14 PM | Person Reportedly Sleeping in Bike Lockers

Officers received a report of a person possibly sleeping inside bicycle lockers at the State Services Building, 1525 Sherman Street.

11:05 PM | Reckless SUV Reported on I-25

A Mercedes-Benz SUV was reported swerving and failing to maintain its lane while traveling northbound on Interstate 25 near milepost 172. The reporting party maintained visual contact and offered assistance.

10:42 PM | Two-Vehicle Crash on Auraria Parkway Overpass

Transportation personnel discussed a possible two-car, non-injury crash on an overpass near Auraria Parkway and Colfax Avenue. Plans were discussed to move the vehicles out of the roadway while awaiting police response.

10:34 PM | Worker Falls Ill at State Capitol Complex

Paramedics responded to the State Capitol complex along East Colfax Avenue after a worker reportedly fell and became ill. Radio traffic indicated the person appeared to be moving in and out of consciousness. Paramedics were reported on scene.

10:26 PM | Possible Narcotics Incident at Sixth and Broadway

Officers responded to a bus shelter near East Sixth Avenue and Broadway, where they encountered one person and requested another unit. Dispatch subsequently changed the call classification to a possible narcotics incident.

ADAMS COUNTY AND AURORA

11:50 PM | Bus Reports Heavy Smoke at 40th and Airport

A bus operator reported unusually heavy smoke coming from beneath the rear portion of a bus near East 40th Avenue and Airport Boulevard in Aurora. The smoke reportedly originated near a rear tire rather than the normal exhaust outlet.

11:24 PM | Rear-End Crash at 88th and Quince

Emergency crews responded to a two-vehicle collision at East 88th Avenue and Quince Street. Damage was described as minor, although one driver reportedly struck her head on the steering wheel. Responders reported one stable patient.

11:14 PM | Cold Exposure Emergency at Colfax and Billings

Aurora emergency crews responded to a reported cold exposure medical incident near East Colfax Avenue and Billings Street. The patient’s condition was not available.

ARAPAHOE COUNTY

11:33 PM | Gas or Chemical Odor at Circle K

Fire crews responded to a possible gas or chemical odor at a Circle K near South Oswego Street in Greenwood Village. The source of the odor was not confirmed.

These incidents were reported through publicly available emergency dispatch communications on November 19 and shortly after midnight on November 20, 2026. Information is preliminary and may change as additional details become available.

🚨 Today, we tell the story of one of the greatest heists in tech history.

A 28 year old paid $18,000 to invent 4 million customers.

JPMorgan bought her company for $175 million. Then the bank ended up paying over $100 million in her legal bills.

In 2017, Charlie Javice launched Frank, a platform that helped college students apply for financial aid. It was a real business, but she wanted it to look much bigger.

She started claiming Frank had over 4 million users. It landed her on Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2019.

In 2021, JPMorgan offered $175 million for the company and its customers. Before closing, the bank asked her to prove the numbers.

Frank had fewer than 300,000 real users.

So she paid a data science professor $18,000 to create over 4 million fake students. Names, emails, birthdates, even income levels. All made up.

JPMorgan closed the deal. Javice walked away with $29 million and a Managing Director role at the bank.

The lie started falling apart when JPMorgan sent a test marketing campaign to Frank's "customers." The results were a disaster.

Then an engineering director testified that Javice had asked him to fake the data the week before the deal closed. He refused because he didn't want to go to prison.

She was arrested in 2023, posted a $2 million bail, and worked as a Pilates instructor in South Florida while she waited for trial.

In March 2025, a jury convicted her on all four counts: bank fraud, securities fraud, wire fraud and conspiracy.

She was sentenced to 85 months in federal prison and ordered to pay $287.5 million in restitution.

But here's the twist.

Because her deal made her a JPMorgan employee, the bank was legally required to cover her legal fees. That bill passed $100 million.

JPMorgan paid to defend the woman who fooled them. https://t.co/cgsfIrvYG5

text:
SURAH AL-JINN
Number of verses: 28 | Period: Mecca (in all likelihood after the journey to Taif) | Pedagogical order: 88
Subject: The Limit of the Unseen — Human Responsibility
Reference Frame: Qur'an Tafsir Reference Protocol v27 | Foundational Axiom: an-Nisa 136 | Epistemic Limit: Allah knows best.
INTRODUCTION: CONTEXT, THE HISTORICAL READING OF THE “JINN”, AND THE EPISTEMOLOGICAL CRISIS
The surah was sent down in the heaviest years of siege of the Meccan period, in all likelihood after the journey to Taif. It was revealed in a time when the Prophet was confronted with pressures from without, with a sense of loneliness from within, and with the systematic campaign of discredit waged by the Meccan oligarchy. As required by article 0b of the Protocol, the historical context of the surah is the key of the interpretation: the Meccan elites, by labeling the Prophet as a “soothsayer” (a diviner, one who gives news of the future) or as “possessed by jinn” (majnun), were trying to tie the source of the message he brought to networks of the unseen, dark, and untrustworthy. Surah al-Jinn is a manifesto that answers this accusation directly, structurally collapses the epistemological crisis of the age, and assigns the source of truth to Allah alone.
The analysis must be begun in the light of an-Nisa 136, the unalterable foundational axiom of the Protocol: faith in Allah, in His Prophet, in the Book sent down upon him, and in the books sent down before. The structure of this verse shows that faith is a continually renewed orientation; to “those who have believed” the command “believe” is given anew. The scope carries the four pillars together: Allah, the Prophet, the Qur'an, and the previous original revelations. A critical distinction must be made here: the Torah and the Gospel to which the Qur'an refers are not the versions shaped by human hands and compiled from the memories of the apostles that are accepted today by church or synagogue authorities. The reference is to the pure, original, tawhid-centered revelations of the time they were first sent down. The Qur'an came down as the verifier, the protector, and the final criterion that separates truth from falsehood (the Furqan) of these original messages. The emphasis of tawhid in Surah al-Jinn directly supports the continuity of this chain of original revelation and the Qur'an's position of protector within this chain.
The concept of “jinn” is not supernatural beings; it is the foreign delegations who concealed their identity to escape the pressure and embargo of the Meccan oligarchy (the intelligence apparatus of the Quraysh), who remained in the darkness, who listened in secret; the leading men of far regions (Nasibin, Yemen) or the early secret sympathizers of Medina (the Ansar).
1. Historical and Siyer Verification: the Theory of “the Hidden Human Beings”
The great majority of the classical tafsirs convey this event as a supernatural miracle, reflecting the mythological perception among the common people (the jinn upon the mountain). But Abu Muslim al-Isfahani (the twelfth-century rationalist exegete) and contemporary academic researchers refuse this reading, drawing attention to the internal consistency of the verses and to the historical context (the Siyer).
The Siyer Context (Protocol 0b): the Prophet, gravely wounded from the journey to Taif, is returning to Mecca under a psychological and sociological blockade (boycott). The Meccan oligarchy (the Quraysh) had wholly cut his contact with the outer world, with the tribes and the leading men, and was applying an “intelligence embargo.” No one could speak with him openly; those who listened to him were being declared “mad” or “sorcerer” and cast out of society.
The group that listened in secret to the Prophet while he recited the Qur'an by night in this valley of “Nakhla” or “Qarnu'l-Manazil” is defined, in the academic literature and the rationalist reading, as “foreign delegations come from far regions who were obliged to conceal their identity, Jewish/Christian scholars (from Nasibin or the region of Yemen), or the elites in search of an early secret alliance (the forerunners of the Ansar of Medina) who feared the pressure of Mecca.”
Why were they called “Jinn” (the hidden)? The Arabic root J-N-N means “to cover, to hide, to remain in darkness, to conceal one's identity.” These delegations, to escape the spy networks of the Meccan oligarchy (of the Quraysh), to avoid a diplomatic crisis or a physical lynching, listened to the Prophet incognito — concealing their identities in the darkness of night, in the hollows of the valleys (the metaphor of “the stations of the heaven / the secret listening posts” in verses 8-9).
The Possibility of the Leading Men of Medina: the leading men of the tribes of Medina (Yathrib), the Aws and the Khazraj, were conducting their first contacts with the Prophet (before the pledges of Aqaba) in the utmost secrecy, because they feared the pressure of Mecca. These “secret listeners / elites in search of a secret alliance,” not wishing to live an open tension with the Meccan oligarchy, escaped the surveillance of the Quraysh and listened to the revelation in the darkness of night. The Qur'an reverses, in an ironic language, the smear propaganda of Mecca, “none but the jinn (madness / invisible powers) listen to him”: “those secret listeners whom you took for 'invisible beings / jinn' (the elites of the far regions, the hidden delegations) surrendered before the rational power of the revelation.”
2. Semantic and Logical Proofs (Protocols 0d and 17)
The internal structure of the verses cries out that these listeners are not ontological “aliens/ghosts” but a sociological group of human beings:
A. “When they returned to their people...” (al-Jinn 11-14): the jinn's returning to their people as warners (nadhirs) is biologically and ontologically impossible. But the secret delegates come from Nasibin, from Yemen, or from Medina's returning to their own people / leading men and saying “We heard a rational truth (a Furqan)” is a historical and sociological reality.
B. “The mosques belong to Allah alone...” (al-Jinn 18): this verse stresses that the public spaces, the diplomatic meeting points, and the houses of worship must be cleansed of the idols / intermediary authorities of the oligarchy. This is the theological approval of a proposal of “public space and alliance” that the secret delegations or the Medinan sympathizers offered to the Prophet.
C. Protocol 17d (Symbolic Language): just as with the Prophet Solomon's listening to the ants (the peasants at the very bottom of society, whose voice is not heard), so the Prophet Muhammad's listening to, and addressing, the persons of “invisible / jinn” status whom Mecca counted as non-existent, who remained in the darkness and were forced into hiding (the secret delegates, the foreign scholars) is the establishing of a revolutionary network of equality and communication.
3. The Axiom of Nisa 136 and Contact with the “Original Revelation”
When this historical reading is joined with the unalterable axiom of the Protocol, Nisa 136, it gains a magnificent epistemological depth.
If these “secret listeners” (the jinn) are Jewish/Christian scholars come from Nasibin or the region of Yemen, or the elites of far tribes possessing knowledge of the original Torah/Gospel, then the reaction they gave upon hearing the Qur'an (verse 2: “We heard a wondrous Qur'an that guides to rushd (to rational maturity / the right)”) is precisely the shock of encountering the original, uncorrupted, pure revelation that Nisa 136 affirms.
The churches and the chief rabbinate seats of the age had corrupted the Torah and the Gospel and produced a theology that ascribed to Allah a “son” or “partners” (the confession of al-Jinn 3-4: “one of us who was foolish would say outrageous things about Allah”). But when these “secret listeners / scholars of the far regions” heard the pure tawhid faith the Qur'an brought (that Allah is free of taking a consort or children — tanZih), they recognized at once that this was the lost or distorted original message.
Their confession, “We shall never again set up any partner to our Lord” (al-Jinn 2), is the breaking away from the human dogmas produced by the church councils or the rabbinical assemblies, and the proclamation of the return to the first and pure revelation of Moses and Jesus (Nisa 136). These scholars, who hid in the darkness to escape the pressure of the Meccan oligarchy, had found the light of the truth.
4. The Breaking of the Epistemological Blockade
The Collapse of the Secret Networks and the Oligarchic Embargo (Verses 1-5):
The Meccan oligarchy had isolated the Prophet and was waging a psychological war, claiming that his message addressed only “dark powers / the jinn” (that is, the marginals outside society, or madness). But the Qur'an structurally collapses this intelligence embargo. “Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn (delegates concealing their identity, remaining in the darkness, fearing the pressure of Mecca / secret Medinan sympathizers / scholars of far regions) listened to the Qur'an...”
This verse is a message of immense consolation and geopolitical victory given to the Prophet and the first believers. The message is this: “They think you alone and besieged. But your voice has passed beyond the intelligence networks of Mecca (the satans' listening to the heaven / Protocols 8-10) and reached the far regions, the hidden elites, and the heirs of the original revelation. They saw how the Furqan you brought (the criterion that separates truth from falsehood) collapsed the superstitions produced by the corrupted authorities of religion (the fools), and they surrendered to the pure tawhid (Nisa 136).”
The first verse of the surah opens with the expression, “Say: It has been revealed to me that a community of the jinn listened to the Qur'an and said: 'Surely we have heard a wondrous Qur'an.'” Article 0g of the Protocol is decisive in the reading of this verse. The root of “jinn” (J-N-N) carries the meaning “to cover, to hide, to remain in the dark.” In the cultural perception of the jahiliyya, the soothsayers claimed to receive knowledge of the unseen from “the jinn.” In the perception of the audience of the age this meant the secret networks of information, the intelligence sources, the invisible strata of society, and the manipulative webs of the soothsayers. The Protocol makes it binding that the concept of jinn be understood not as an ontologically independent species (an alien, ghost, or independent spiritual category of being) but as a near companionship and role that leads a person astray, that whispers, that produces secret knowledge, that manipulates. Just as in the story of the Prophet Solomon's speaking with the ants, where what is in question is not a literal dialogue with insects but the symbolic telling of the hearing, by a just ruler, of the rights of the peasants living in the Valley of the Ants, at the lowest stratum of the people, whose voice is not heard; so the “listening of the jinn” in Surah al-Jinn is not a literal supernatural event but the symbolic telling of the surrender, before the rational truth of the Qur'an, of the secret networks of the age, the manipulative webs, and the soothsayers' sources of information. The expression “wondrous Qur'an” (Qur'anan 'ajaban) proclaims that even these hidden networks felt astonishment and admiration before the logical consistency, the universal moral message, and the epistemological soundness of the Qur'an — that is, that the truth is not in the monopoly of the dark webs, but that, as an evident Furqan, it penetrates to everyone.
The second verse declares that this Qur'an “guides to the right” (yahdi ila'r-rushd), and that they have believed in it and will never again set up partners to their Lord. The word “rushd” carries the meaning of the maturing of the reason, the capacity to find the right path, the conscious orientation. This is directly connected with the concept of “lubb” (the enlightened intellect) in article 6d of the Protocol. The secret networks, the manipulative webs, and the sources of whispering, accepting the structure of the Qur'an that leads to rushd (to rational maturity), abandon the setting up of partners (the associating of partners with Allah). Shirk here is not only the worshipping of idols; as the Protocol defines it, it is the placing of the ego, the desires, worldly interests, hidden centers of power, or other authorities before the teaching of Allah. The soothsayers' claim to receive knowledge “from the jinn” was the raising of these secret networks to the position of partners in divine knowledge; the Qur'an structurally collapses this partnership.
The third and fourth verses establish the tanZih dimension of tawhid: “The majesty of our Lord is exalted; He has taken neither a consort nor a child.” This expression is the direct application of the binding principle of tanZih in article 20a of the Protocol: Allah is the one who creates and is perfect with absolute perfection; time, space, weakness, mortality, need, and dependence are the attributes of the created, not of the Creator. The expressions “taking a consort” and “taking a child” are a direct refusal of the deviations seen in the idolatrous Arab theology of the age (the claim that the angels were the daughters of Allah) and in the human interpretations later added to the previous traditions of revelation (the corrupting of the pure tawhid of the original Gospel and the producing of the myth of the divine son). While the Qur'an re-establishes the pure tawhid in the original revelations affirmed by Nisa 136, it sifts out the human layers added afterward. The word “sefih” (foolish, deficient of mind, destitute of thought) in the fourth verse defines the epistemological position of those who make outrageous claims about Allah: these are they who reduce the divine authority to human categories, who set idols, hidden powers, or ideological leaders in the place of Allah.
The fifth verse continues with the expression, “We thought indeed that men and jinn would never speak falsehood against Allah.” The soothsayers, the rabbis, and the councils of the church (their priests) were presenting, ascribing it to Allah, the knowledge they claimed to receive “from the jinn” (from the secret sources of information); and society believed that this knowledge came from Allah. But with the coming down of the Qur'an it came to light that these secret sources had spoken falsehood in the name of Allah, had produced fabricated knowledge, and had manipulated the people. The expression “men and jinn” covers both the open (human) and the hidden (jinn) manipulators; both categories possess the capacity of speaking falsehood against Allah, and the Qur'an lays this capacity bare.
THE HISTORICAL DECIPHERMENT OF VERSE 5 OF SURAH AL-JINN: THE MECHANISM OF “SPEAKING FALSEHOOD IN THE NAME OF ALLAH” AND THE ACTORS OF MANIPULATION
Reference Protocol: the Qur'an Tafsir Reference Protocol v27 (articles 0b, 0d, 0g, 17, 18, 26, and the Axiom of Nisa 136).
The Text of the Verse and Its Epistemological Frame
The fifth verse of Surah al-Jinn says: “Ve enna zannenna en len tekule'l-insu ve'l-cinnu alallahi keziba” — “We thought indeed that men and jinn would never speak falsehood against Allah.”
This sentence is a most shattering epistemological confession. The “secret listeners” of the age (the delegations in the role of jinn, the scholars of far regions, the secret sympathizers) confess that they had lived before with this assumption: “No one who speaks in the name of Allah speaks falsely.” If the soothsayer says “I received it from Allah,” if the rabbi says “the Torah says thus,” if the priest says “this is the decree of the Gospel,” the truth of these words could not be doubted, they supposed. But when they listened to the rational, shattering, and pure tawhid message of the Qur'an, they understood what a dangerous delusion this assumption had been.
The unalterable axiom of the Protocol, Nisa 136, sets here a key distinction: the Torah and the Gospel that the Qur'an affirms are not the versions shaped by human hands and dogmatized by the decisions of councils that are read today in synagogues or churches. The reference is to the first, pure, original tawhid message revealed to Moses and to Jesus. But this original message was systematically manipulated through history by certain actors. Verse 5 is precisely the decipherment of this manipulation: to speak falsehood in the name of Allah is to instrumentalize the divine authority for human interests.
The Category of “Men”: the Manipulation of the Open Authorities
The expression “men” (al-ins) in the verse covers the religious actors who stand in a position legitimate, visible, and authoritative in the eyes of society. These are not “hidden” (jinn) but “open” (human) manipulators; they speak from the pulpit, from the prayer niche, from the synagogue, or from the temple. The Qur'an documents the manipulation mechanisms of these actors concretely in more than one surah:
The Soothsayers (the Arab Tradition of the Jahiliyya): the soothsayers of the jahiliyya period were presenting, ascribing it to Allah, the knowledge they claimed to receive “from the jinn” (from secret sources of information, from intelligence networks). Society did not question the source of this knowledge; for the soothsayer was speaking “in the name of Allah.” This is the nakedest form of the deed of “speaking falsehood against Allah” in verse 5: the attributing of fabricated information to the divine authority. The Qur'an structurally collapses this practice with the metaphor of the “shihab” (blaze) in al-Mulk 3-5: the truth is closed to the manipulation of the soothsayers; the claim of “stealing news from heaven” is invalid.
The Rabbis and the Doctors of Religion (the Rabbinic Tradition): the Qur'an documents this manipulation openly in Al-e Imran 78: “There is a party among them who twist their tongues with the Book, that you may suppose it to be part of the Book, though it is not part of the Book; and they say, 'It is from Allah,' though it is not from Allah, and they speak falsehood against Allah while they know.” This verse gives the historical counterpart of the deed of “men's speaking falsehood against Allah” in verse 5. The rabbis, adding to the original text of the Torah their human interpretations, the Talmudic traditions, and their own fatwas, presented these as “the word of Allah.” In al-Baqara 79 this is expressed yet more sharply: “Woe to those who write the Book with their hands and then sell it for a small price! Woe to them for what their hands have written!” Here the “small price” is the converting of religious authority into economic and political rent. In at-Tawba 34, with the expression “the rabbis and the monks consume the goods of the people unjustly and turn them from the way of Allah,” the converting of religious authority into “a vehicle of transfer of wealth” (Protocol 31e: Legal Corruption and Bribery) is cursed.

Here are some scams I have experienced.

Mumbai: Hotel claims rooms are not available though i have pre-booked on booking dot com. Offers another hotel at same price. But new hotel is a shady lodge that should cost less than half. 

Delhi: Prepaid taxi fare is 250 rupees.  Booth operator takes a 1000 rupee note from you (this was in 2008, pre-demonetization, pre-uber) and through sleight of hand shows you a 100 rupee note and says you made a mistake. So pay him 150 more. I sadly fell for this scam twice. Once in Delhi and 5 years later in Istanbul.

Bangalore: Airport taxi guy has a fake app that looks like an official app but isnt. You pay double fare on reaching destination.

Goa: Taxi guy at Madgaon station told me that the hotel i booked has shut down and he will help me find a new hotel.

Kolkata: Random shopkeepers and touts outside Kalighat temple will offer you "VIP darshan" for 1000 rupees and claim normal queue takes 3 hours. It actually takes less than an hour. 

Ajmer: Every shop near the dargah is a tout offering "VIP visit." Also, not a scam but the beggars there are the most persistent i have ever encountered.

Ooty/Munnar: Those "home made" chocolates are actually mass produced in factories.

Mumbai: Random touts at the Haji Ali causeway will tell you that you need to leave your shoes with them (for a fee) and you cannot oroceed further otherwise. Ignore them. You can leave your shoes for free at the entrance of the shrine.

Halebidu: The shoe attendant charges double of what is the actual sanctioned govt rate. He has an L1 tender and is heavily scamming you. If you have a car, leave your shoes there.

Ahmedabad: Hotel promises a full breakfast spread including eggs, corn flakes, fruits, etc. But theres a huge low budget tour group at breafast whose package has only poha and aloo paratha and so they give you only that much. 

Dharwad/Hubli: Every sweet shop is Mishra Peda and wvery restaurant is Kamat. Everyone claims to be the OG.

Mysore: Hundreds of Kaveri silk emporiums. All fake and giving commissions to the auto/taxi guy who brought you there. The OG is called Cauvery and very few people end up there.

Gokarna/Varanasi: Cafes and guest houses will tell you they are full. Actually they dont want Indians there and want to maintain a "whites-only" - business. Most of their clients are Zionist murderers discovering Yoga and spirituality.

Every major airport in the world: One guy wearing an official looking badge will approach you and tell you he is an airport official and will help you get a taxi/hotel. He is actually a tout and will rip you off.
